# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer A JWT signed using your CDP API Key Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the [Generate Bearer Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-bearer-token) section of our Authentication docs for information on how to generate your Bearer Token.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer A JWT signed using the developer's own JWT private key (in the case of JWT authentication), or an end user JWT signed by CDP, encoded in base64. This is used for End User Account APIs.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: none This security scheme is used for APIs that do not require authentication, such as End User Auth flows used to initiate authentication or public, read-only endpoints.

* API Key (webhookSignature)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Hook0-Signature**, in: header. HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body, computed using your webhook secret. Webhook receivers should always verify this header before processing the event. The header value is hex-encoded and prefixed by the algorithm and timestamp, e.g. `t=1700000000,v1=abc123...` (refer to the Webhook Security docs for the exact verification algorithm).

This scheme applies to webhook delivery (outbound POSTs from CDP to your endpoint), not to inbound CDP API requests.

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-accounts">Accounts</h1>

The Accounts APIs enable developers to create and manage accounts for their Entity and for their Customers. An Account is a container that holds assets and can be used for transacting. Accounts can be of different types including entity accounts, prime accounts, and business accounts. Use `GET /v2/accounts/{accountId}/products` to discover the spot products available to trade for an account (valid `productId`s to pass when creating an order).

## List accounts

<a id="opIdlistFoundationAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/accounts`

List all accounts. The API will return all accounts that the API Key has Permissions to access. You can filter the results by using query parameters, which will be treated as a single conjunction (i.e. AND). Results are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first).

<h3 id="list-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return per page.|
|pageToken|query|string|false|The token for the next page of resources, if any.|
|owner|query|[string]|false|Filter accounts by owner. Values can be specific Owner IDs or owner type wildcards. Multiple values can be combined as a comma-separated list.<br><br>**Specific Owner IDs:**<br>* `entity_<uuid>` - Accounts owned by a specific entity<br>* `customer_<uuid>` - Accounts owned by a specific customer<br><br>**Owner type wildcards:**<br>* `entity` - All entity-owned accounts<br>* `customer` - All customer-owned accounts<br><br>**Examples:**<br>* `owner=customer_af29...` - A specific customer's accounts<br>* `owner=customer` - All customer accounts<br>* `owner=entity,customer_af29...` - Entity accounts and a specific customer's accounts<br>* When omitted, accounts with any owner are returned.|
|type|query|[AccountType](#schemaaccounttype)|false|Filter accounts by account type. When omitted, accounts of any type are returned. Combined with `owner` using AND.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|prime|
|type|business|
|type|cdp|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
      "type": "prime",
      "owner": "entity_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
      "name": "My Business Account",
      "createdAt": "2023-10-08T14:30:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "2023-10-08T14:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "nextPageToken": "eyJsYXN0X2lkIjogImFiYzEyMyIsICJ0aW1lc3RhbXAiOiAxNzA3ODIzNzAxfQ=="
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Invalid query parameters."
}
```

<h3 id="list-accounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successfully listed accounts.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-accounts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounts|[[Account](#schemaaccount)]|true|none|The list of accounts.|
|nextPageToken|string|false|none|The token for the next page of items, if any.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKeyAuth
</aside>

## Create account

<a id="opIdcreateFoundationAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My Business Account"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/accounts`

Create an account. Two ownership modes are supported:

- **Entity-owned**: when `owner` is omitted, the account is owned by the
  Entity making the request. Returns an account with `owner: entity_<uuid>`.
  Omit `compliance`; it has no effect for Entity-owned accounts.

- **Customer-owned**: pass a Customer ID as `owner`
  (e.g. `customer_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114`). The Customer
  must have the `custodyCrypto`, `custodyFiat`, and `custodyStablecoin`
  capabilities enabled, otherwise the request is rejected with
  `customer_not_authorized` (HTTP 403). `compliance.requesterIpAddress`
  is required; use the IP address of the end-customer who initiated the
  request (not the partner server's IP).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My Business Account"
}
```

<h3 id="create-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|body|body|[CreateAccountRequest](#schemacreateaccountrequest)|true|none|
|» owner|body|object|false|The Owner of the Account to create.<br>* If omitted, the account will be owned by the Entity making the request.<br>* If the account is for a customer, the value will be a Customer ID,<br>  e.g. `customer_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114`.<br><br>* Further, the corresponding Customer must have all of the following capabilities enabled:<br>  - `custodyCrypto`<br>  - `custodyFiat`<br>  - `custodyStablecoin`.|
|» name|body|[AccountName](#schemaaccountname)|false|An optional name for the account. Must be 1-64 characters and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and spaces.|
|» compliance|body|[Compliance](#schemacompliance)|false|Required when `owner` is a Customer ID; omit for Entity-owned accounts.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
  "type": "cdp",
  "owner": "entity_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
  "name": "My Business Account",
  "createdAt": "2023-10-08T14:30:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2023-10-08T14:30:00Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Invalid account creation request."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "customer_not_authorized",
  "errorMessage": "Customer is not authorized for one or more capabilities required by this action.",
  "unauthorizedCapabilities": [
    "custodyCrypto",
    "custodyFiat",
    "custodyStablecoin"
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "idempotency_error",
  "errorMessage": "Idempotency key '8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324' was already used with a different request payload. Please try again with a new idempotency key."
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "service_unavailable",
  "errorMessage": "Service unavailable. Please try again later."
}
```

<h3 id="create-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successfully created account.|[Account](#schemaaccount)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Customer is not authorized for one or more capabilities required by this action.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Idempotency key conflict.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The endpoint cannot serve the request right now, either because the API is in an unintended outage (`service_unavailable` — dependency failure, deploy issue) or because an operator has intentionally disabled this specific endpoint via a kill switch (`endpoint_unavailable`). Clients should dispatch on `errorType`: `service_unavailable` is typically transient and safe to retry, while `endpoint_unavailable` may persist until an operator re-enables the endpoint.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKeyAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-customers">Customers</h1>

The Customers APIs enable developers to create and manage their end-user customers. Customers can be individuals or businesses and have various capabilities like sending/receiving fiat and crypto, trading, etc. Customer information includes KYC/compliance data, verification requirements, and capability management.

## List customers

<a id="opIdlistCustomers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/customers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/customers`

List all customers. The API will return all customers that the API Key has
permissions to access. Results are not returned in any guaranteed order.


<h3 id="list-customers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Create a customer

<a id="opIdcreateCustomer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/customers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "individual",
    "individual": {
      "firstName": "Jane",
      "lastName": "Doe",
      "address": {
        "line1": "500 Main St",
        "city": "Boston",
        "state": "MA",
        "postCode": "02108",
        "countryCode": "US"
      }
    },
    "capabilities": {
      "custodyCrypto": {
        "requested": true
      },
      "transferCrypto": {
        "requested": true
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/customers`

Create a new customer record. You can optionally request capabilities
and submit verification requirements in the same request.

This endpoint supports creating a customer with:
- Minimal data (customer type only)
- Capability requests
- KYC data submission
- Combined request for capability and required info for verification


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "individual",
  "individual": {
    "firstName": "Jane",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "address": {
      "line1": "500 Main St",
      "city": "Boston",
      "state": "MA",
      "postCode": "02108",
      "countryCode": "US"
    }
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "custodyCrypto": {
      "requested": true
    },
    "transferCrypto": {
      "requested": true
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|

## Get customer requirements

<a id="opIdgetCustomerRequirements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/customers/requirements?customerType=individual&capabilities=custodyCrypto&capabilities=transferCrypto' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/customers/requirements`

Preview the requirements a hypothetical customer of the given
`customerType` and jurisdiction would need to satisfy to enable the
requested `capabilities`, without creating a customer record.
Partner onboarding UIs can use this to render the collection flow
before any customer state exists.

Today this endpoint only previews the Terms of Service requirement:
the response's `RequirementsMap` will only ever contain a `tos` key.
Other requirement families (PII / CDD inputs) are not yet available
through this endpoint; use `POST /v2/customers` or
`PUT /v2/customers/{customerId}` to discover those via
`Customer.requirements`.

Only `customerType: individual` customers resident in or citizens
of the US are currently supported; every other combination returns
`400 invalid_request`.


<h3 id="get-customer-requirements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customerType|query|[CustomerType](#schemacustomertype)|true|The type of the hypothetical customer.|
|capabilities|query|[[CapabilityName](#schemacapabilityname)]|true|The capabilities the hypothetical customer would request.<br>Repeat the parameter to specify multiple capabilities, for<br>example `capabilities=custodyCrypto&capabilities=transferCrypto`.<br>|
|countryCode|query|[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)|false|The hypothetical customer's country of residence. At least one<br>of `countryCode` or `citizenship` is required. When both are<br>present, `countryCode` takes precedence.<br>|
|citizenship|query|[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)|false|The hypothetical customer's citizenship. At least one of<br>`countryCode` or `citizenship` is required.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|customerType|individual|
|capabilities|custodyCrypto|
|capabilities|custodyFiat|
|capabilities|custodyStablecoin|
|capabilities|tradeCrypto|
|capabilities|tradeStablecoin|
|capabilities|transferCrypto|
|capabilities|transferFiat|
|capabilities|transferStablecoin|

```json
    "status": "due",

      "custodyCrypto",
      "transferCrypto"
    ],
    "tosVersions": [
      {
        "versionId": "us_individual_2026-05-29",
        "languages": [
          "en"
        ],
        "url": "https://www.coinbase.com/legal/user-agreements-third-party-provider"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Invalid request. Please check the request parameters."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "unauthorized",
  "errorMessage": "The request is not properly authenticated."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

> 502 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "bad_gateway",
  "errorMessage": "Bad gateway. Please try again later."
}
```

|400|Bad Request|Invalid request. Distinct causes include a missing required<br>parameter, both `countryCode` and `citizenship` omitted, an<br>unrecognized `capabilities` value, and a<br>`(customerType, jurisdiction)` combination that is not yet<br>supported (currently only `individual` customers resident in or<br>citizens of the US).|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

## Update a customer

<a id="opIdupdateCustomerById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/customers/customer_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "capabilities": {
      "custodyFiat": {
        "requested": true
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/customers/{customerId}`

Update customer information and/or request capability changes.
This endpoint supports partial updates. Provide only the fields you wish to change.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "custodyFiat": {
      "requested": true
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customerId|path|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|true|The ID of the customer.|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|body|body|[UpdateCustomerRequest](#schemaupdatecustomerrequest)|false|Customer fields to update. All fields are optional; omit a field to<br>leave it unchanged.<br>|
|» type|body|object|false|The type of the customer. Required on create; accepted but ignored on<br>update.<br>|
|» capabilities|body|object|false|Capabilities to request for the customer.|
|» » custodyCrypto|body|object|false|Hold cryptocurrency in a Coinbase custodial account.|
|» » » requested|body|boolean|true|Whether to request this capability.|
|» » custodyFiat|body|object|false|Hold fiat currency in a Coinbase custodial account.|
|» » » requested|body|boolean|true|Whether to request this capability.|
|» » custodyStablecoin|body|object|false|Hold stablecoin in a Coinbase custodial account.|

## Delete a customer

<a id="opIddeleteCustomerById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/customers/customer_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/customers/{customerId}`

Initiates deletion of the customer and all associated data. This operation
is idempotent — repeated calls for an already-deleted customer return 204.
A 404 is returned only when no customer with the given ID exists for the
caller's entity.


<h3 id="delete-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|customerId|path|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|true|The ID of the customer.|

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-deposit-destinations">Deposit Destinations</h1>

Deposit Destinations allow you to manage where funds can be deposited into your accounts.

## Crypto Deposit Destinations

Crypto deposit destinations are cryptocurrency addresses that you can generate and fetch via the API. Once created, these addresses can receive cryptocurrency payments on their specified network. By default, incoming funds are credited to your account balance (`target.accountId`); you can instead route funds directly to an external onchain address by setting `target` to an onchain address (`target.address`, `target.network`, `target.asset`, and optionally `target.destinationTag`).

**Metadata:**
You can attach metadata to any deposit destination you create to track the purpose or source of deposits.


**Example (target: account balance):**
```json
{
  "depositDestinationId": "depositDestination_123",
  "accountId": "account_456",
  "type": "crypto",
  "crypto": {
    "network": "base",
    "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e"
  },
  "target": {
    "accountId": "account_789",
    "asset": "usd"
  },
  "status": "active",
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_789",
    "reference": "order-12345"
  }
}
```
**Example (target: onchain address):**
```json
{
  "depositDestinationId": "depositDestination_123",
  "accountId": "account_456",
  "type": "crypto",
  "crypto": {
    "network": "base",
    "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e"
  },
  "target": {
    "address": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    "network": "base",
    "asset": "usdc"
  },
  "status": "active",
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_789",
    "reference": "order-12345"
  }
}
```
Use the list endpoint to retrieve all deposit destinations.

## Fiat Deposit Destinations

<Warning>
Fiat deposit destinations are currently in **private beta** and require account enablement. Contact your Coinbase representative for access. Fields and behavior may change before general availability.
</Warning>

Fiat deposit destinations are bank accounts provisioned on your behalf that let an account receive USD deposits over a supported payment rail (for example, ACH). Each fiat deposit destination represents a single bank account at a single banking partner and is keyed by `accountType` (for example, `us_bank`).

**Example:**
```json
{
  "depositDestinationId": "depositDestination_cf4958d2-b068-6bf9-da01-eee44f157336",
  "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
  "type": "fiat",
  "status": "pending",
  "fiat": {
    "accountType": "us_bank",
    "currency": "usd",
    "bankName": "Citibank N.A.",
    "beneficiaryName": "John Smith",
    "routingNumber": "987654321",
    "accountNumber": "123456789",
    "bankAddress": "399 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10022",
    "supportedRails": ["ach", "fedwire"]
  },
  "target": {
    "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
    "asset": "usdc"
  }
}
```
Use the create endpoint to provision a fiat deposit destination for an account.

## List deposit destinations

<a id="opIdlistDepositDestinations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/deposit-destinations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/deposit-destinations`

List deposit destinations. You can optionally filter the results by type, account ID, network, cryptocurrency address, or status. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first).

|accountId|query|[AccountId](#schemaaccountid)|false|Filter deposit destinations by account ID.|
|address|query|string|false|Filter deposit destinations by the cryptocurrency address.|
|type|query|[DepositDestinationType](#schemadepositdestinationtype)|false|Filter deposit destinations by type.|
|network|query|string|false|Filter deposit destinations by network.|
|status|query|[DepositDestinationStatus](#schemadepositdestinationstatus)|false|Filter deposit destinations by status.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return per page.|
|pageToken|query|string|false|The token for the next page of resources, if any.|

|status|active|
|status|inactive|
|status|pending|

## Create deposit destination

<a id="opIdcreateDepositDestination"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/deposit-destinations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
    "type": "crypto",
    "crypto": {
      "network": "base"
    },
    "target": {
      "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
      "asset": "usd"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "customer_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
      "reference": "order-12345"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/deposit-destinations`

Create a new deposit destination for an account. Two types are supported:

- `crypto` (public): provisions a cryptocurrency address on the requested
  network. The returned `crypto.address` is the deposit address; funds
  sent to it are credited to the `target` account in the specified asset.
  For Customer-owned accounts, the Customer must have the `custodyCrypto`
  and `custodyStablecoin` capabilities enabled.


- `fiat` (private-beta): provisions a bank
  account at a CDP banking partner. The server picks the account type
  (e.g. `us_bank`) and supported payment rails based on the account's
  eligibility; pass `fiat.paymentRail` to influence partner selection.
  The returned `fiat` object contains the bank account details the
  depositor needs to send funds. For Customer-owned accounts, the Customer
  must have the `custodyFiat` capability enabled. Requires account
  enablement — contact your Coinbase representative for access. Fields
  and behavior may change before general availability.


For Customer-owned accounts not authorized for the required capabilities,
the request is rejected with `customer_not_authorized` (HTTP 403).


The created destination's `status` starts as `pending` for fiat (it
becomes `active` once the partner provisioning callback completes) and
`active` for crypto.

```json
  "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
  "type": "crypto",
  "crypto": {
    "network": "base"
  },
  "target": {
    "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
    "asset": "usd"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
    "reference": "order-12345"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-disbursements">Disbursements</h1>

Send funds from a CDP account you own to a Coinbase user account or an onchain address. Use disbursements for standalone refunds, rebates, and other payouts that are not associated with a payment session.

## Lifecycle

Disbursements are created with `pending` status and transition to `succeeded` or `failed`. Successful disbursements include `onchainTransactions`; failed disbursements include `error` details.

Subscribe to `acceptance.disbursement.pending`, `acceptance.disbursement.succeeded`, and `acceptance.disbursement.failed` webhook events to receive status updates.

## List disbursements

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/disbursements`

Creates a disbursement from a CDP account you own to a Coinbase user account or an onchain address. Returns the disbursement with `pending` status while processing continues asynchronously.

> Body parameter

```json
{

    "accountId": "account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
    "asset": "usdc"
  },

  },

  "asset": "usdc",
  "reason": "Goodwill disbursement for delayed shipment.",
  "externalReferenceId": "disbursement-2026-04-1234",
  "customerDisplay": {
    "merchantName": "Acme Store",
    "referenceCode": "REF-ABC123"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_12345",
    "order_id": "order_67890"
  }
}
```

|body|body|[CreateDisbursementRequest](#schemacreatedisbursementrequest)|false|none|
|» source|body|object|true|The source from which to fund the disbursement.|

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-end-user-account-management">End User Account Management</h1>

The End User Account Management APIs enable developers to manage the accounts belonging to their end users. End user accounts are typically created by end users themselves when they sign in to the developer's application via the CDP Web SDK. However, developers also have the option of creating end user accounts on behalf of their end users. Critically, developers do not have the ability to sign transactions or messages on behalf of the end user; only end users can do this.

End User Account Management APIs are accessed by the developer's servers and authenticated by the developer's CDP API key.

## List end users

<a id="opIdlistEndUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/end-users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/end-users`

Lists the end users belonging to the developer's CDP Project.
By default, the response is sorted by creation date in ascending order and paginated to 20 users per page.

<h3 id="list-end-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The number of end users to return per page.|
|pageToken|query|string|false|The token for the desired page of end users. Will be empty if there are no more end users to fetch.|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Sort end users. Defaults to ascending order (oldest first).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|createdAt=asc|
|sort|createdAt=desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "endUsers": [
```

## Create end user

<a id="opIdcreateEndUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/end-users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'X-Wallet-Auth: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOjEyMywicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIiwiZXhwIjoxNzAxOTgwMDAwfQ.HWvMTKmCCTxHaxjvZyLaC6UQ6TV3ErTDWBf7zmdH0Lw' \
  -d '{
    "authenticationMethods": [
      {
        "type": "email",
        "email": "user@example.com"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/end-users`

Creates an end user. An end user is an entity that can own CDP EVM accounts, EVM smart accounts, and/or Solana accounts. 1 or more authentication methods must be associated with an end user. By default, no accounts are created unless the optional `evmAccount` and/or `solanaAccount` fields are provided.
This API is intended to be used by the developer's own backend, and is authenticated using the developer's CDP API key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authenticationMethods": [
    {
      "type": "email",
      "email": "user@example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-end-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|true|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» userId|body|string|false|A stable, unique identifier for the end user. The `userId` must be unique across all end users in the developer's CDP Project. It must be between 1 and 100 characters long and can only contain alphanumeric characters and hyphens.<br><br>If `userId` is not provided in the request, the server will generate a random UUID.|
|» authenticationMethods|body|[AuthenticationMethods](#schemaauthenticationmethods)|true|The list of valid authentication methods linked to the end user.|
|» evmAccount|body|object|false|Configuration for creating an EVM account for the end user.|
|» » createSmartAccount|body|boolean|false|If true, creates an EVM smart account and a default EVM EOA account as the owner. If false, only a EVM EOA account is created.|
|» » enableSpendPermissions|body|boolean|false|If true, enables spend permissions for the EVM smart account.|
|» solanaAccount|body|object|false|Configuration for creating a Solana account for the end user.|
|» » createSmartAccount|body|boolean|false|Only false is a valid option since currently smart accounts on Solana are not supported.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "userId": "user-001",
  "authenticationMethods": [
    {
      "type": "email",
      "email": "user@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "evmAccounts": [],
  "evmAccountObjects": [],
  "evmSmartAccounts": [],
  "evmSmartAccountObjects": [],
  "solanaAccounts": [],
  "solanaAccountObjects": [],
  "createdAt": "2025-11-17T10:00:00Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "At least one authentication method must be provided."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "unauthorized",
  "errorMessage": "Wallet authentication error."
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "payment_method_required",
  "errorMessage": "A valid payment method is required to complete this operation. Please add a payment method to your account at https://portal.cdp.coinbase.com."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "idempotency_error",
  "errorMessage": "Idempotency key '8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324' was already used with a different request payload. Please try again with a new idempotency key."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

|400|Bad Request|Invalid request.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

`POST /v2/end-users/auth/validate-token`

Validates the end user's access token and returns the end user's information. Returns an error if the access token is invalid or expired.

This API is intended to be used by the developer's own backend, and is authenticated using the developer's CDP API key.

```json
}
```

## Look up end users by identity

<a id="opIdlookupEndUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/end-users/lookup \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/end-users/lookup`

Looks up end users. Exactly one lookup type must be provided per request:

- **email**: searches across all email-based authentication methods
  (email, Google, Apple, GitHub). May return multiple end users if the
  same email address appears across different auth methods.

- **oauthProvider + oauthSubject**: looks up a user by their OAuth
  provider and subject (the `sub` claim from the provider's ID token).
  Both params must be provided together.

- **phoneNumber**: looks up a user by their SMS-verified phone number.
- **siweAddress**: looks up a user by the Ethereum address they authenticated
  with via Sign In With Ethereum (EIP-4361).


Returns all matching end users. If no end users match, an empty array is returned.

This API is intended to be used by the developer's own backend, and is authenticated using the developer's CDP API key.

<h3 id="look-up-end-users-by-identity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|query|[Email](#schemaemail)|false|The email address to search for across all email-based authentication methods.|
|oauthProvider|query|[OAuth2ProviderType](#schemaoauth2providertype)|false|The OAuth provider to search by. Must be provided together with oauthSubject.|
|oauthSubject|query|string|false|The OAuth subject (the `sub` claim from the provider's ID token). Must be provided together with oauthProvider.|
|phoneNumber|query|[PhoneNumber](#schemaphonenumber)|false|The E.164-formatted phone number to search for. Must be URL-encoded when passed as a query parameter (e.g. `+14155552671` → `%2B14155552671`).|
|siweAddress|query|[BlockchainAddress](#schemablockchainaddress)|false|The ERC-55 checksummed Ethereum address to search for. Looks up a user by the address they authenticated with via Sign In With Ethereum (EIP-4361).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|oauthProvider|google|
|oauthProvider|apple|
|oauthProvider|x|
|oauthProvider|telegram|
|oauthProvider|github|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "endUsers": [
    {
      "userId": "user-001",
      "authenticationMethods": [
        {
          "type": "email",
          "email": "user@example.com"
        }
      ],
      "evmAccounts": [],
      "evmAccountObjects": [],
      "evmSmartAccounts": [],
      "evmSmartAccountObjects": [],
      "solanaAccounts": [],
      "solanaAccountObjects": [],
      "createdAt": "2025-11-17T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Exactly one lookup type must be provided: email, phoneNumber, siweAddress, or oauthProvider+oauthSubject."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "unauthorized",
  "errorMessage": "The request is not properly authenticated."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

<h3 id="look-up-end-users-by-identity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successfully looked up end users.|Inline|

`POST /v2/end-users/import`

Imports an existing private key for an end user into the developer's CDP Project. The private key must be encrypted using the CDP SDK's encryption scheme before being sent to this endpoint. This API should be called from the [CDP SDK](https://github.com/coinbase/cdp-sdk) to ensure that the associated private key is properly encrypted.

This endpoint allows developers to import existing keys for their end users, supporting both EVM and Solana key types. The end user must have at least one authentication method configured.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "userId": "user-001",
  "authenticationMethods": [
    {
      "type": "email",
      "email": "user@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "encryptedPrivateKey": "U2FsdGVkX1+vupppZksvRf5X5YgHq4+da+Q4qf51+Q4=",
  "keyType": "evm"
}
```

<h3 id="import-end-user-private-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|true|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» userId|body|string|true|A stable, unique identifier for the end user. The `userId` must be unique across all end users in the developer's CDP Project. It must be between 1 and 100 characters long and can only contain alphanumeric characters and hyphens.|
|» authenticationMethods|body|[AuthenticationMethods](#schemaauthenticationmethods)|true|The list of valid authentication methods linked to the end user.|
|» encryptedPrivateKey|body|string|true|The base64-encoded, encrypted private key to import. The private key must be encrypted using the CDP SDK's encryption scheme. This is a 32-byte raw private key.|
|» keyType|body|string|true|The type of key being imported. Determines what type of account will be associated for the end user.|

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-end-user-accounts">End User Accounts</h1>

The End User Accounts APIs enable end users to directly create, manage, and use their accounts. They are typically accessed via the CDP Web SDK, which handles end-user authentication and Temporary Wallet Secret management on behalf of the developer. The End User Accounts APIs offer end users full control over their accounts, including the ability to sign transactions and messages, and to export their accounts' private keys.

## Delegated Signing

Delegated signing allows developers to sign and send transactions on behalf of an end user without requiring the end user to be present at signing time. This is useful for background operations, automated workflows, and scenarios where the developer's server needs to act on the end user's behalf.

To use delegated signing, the end user must first create a short-lived **delegation grant** by authenticating with their access token and Temporary Wallet Secret. The grant specifies an `expiresAt` timestamp that defines how long the developer is authorized to sign on the end user's behalf.

Once a delegation grant is active, the developer's server can use its CDP API key to perform signing operations for that end user. The delegation middleware transparently validates that an active (non-expired, non-revoked) grant exists for the `{project, user}` pair before allowing the operation to proceed.

**Grant lifecycle:**

  - Delegation grants are scoped to a single project and end user pair.
  - Grants are time-bounded by the `expiresAt` timestamp and are automatically cleaned up after expiration.
  - Grants can be revoked early by either the end user (using their access token and TWS) or the
    developer (using their API key), via the `RevokeDelegationForEndUser` endpoint.
  - Only one active grant can exist per `{project, user}` pair at a given time.

## List borrow products

<a id="opIdlistEvmBorrowProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/evm/borrow-products \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/embedded-wallet-api/evm/borrow-products`

Lists the borrow products available across all supported networks and protocols. If a network and/or protocol query parameter is supplied, then borrow products are filtered and returned accordingly.
A borrow product is a protocol-native representation of a borrowable market, describing the venue that hosts it, the assets that can be borrowed or posted as collateral, and their collateral and debt capabilities. For example, a Morpho Blue market that lends USDC against cbBTC.

<h3 id="list-borrow-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|network|query|[BorrowProductNetwork](#schemaborrowproductnetwork)|false|The EVM network name to list borrow products for.|
|protocol|query|[BorrowProductProtocol](#schemaborrowproductprotocol)|false|The lending protocol whose borrow products to list.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return per page.|
|pageToken|query|string|false|The token for the next page of resources, if any.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|network|base|
|protocol|morpho_blue|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "borrowProducts": [
    {
      "borrowProductId": "bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df",
      "network": "base",
      "name": "mGLO / USDC",
      "venue": {
        "venueId": "bp_venue_2978db31-f1ff-570f-8329-6e37d6cae04e",
        "entrypointAddress": "0xbbbbbbbbbb9cc5e90e3b3af64bdaf62c37eeffcb",
        "name": "Morpho Blue base-mainnet"
      },
      "assets": [
        {
          "assetId": "bp_asset_7426b5c4-a556-5005-8fee-eb156d491aef",
          "token": {
```

## Get a borrow product

<a id="opIdgetEvmBorrowProduct"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/evm/borrow-products/bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/embedded-wallet-api/evm/borrow-products/{borrowProductId}`

Gets a single borrow product by its ID.
The ID is a stable identifier that uniquely identifies a single borrow product based on the product's onchain parameters. A borrow product is a protocol-native representation of a borrowable market, describing the venue that hosts it and the assets that participate in it together with their collateral and debt capabilities.

<h3 id="get-a-borrow-product-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|borrowProductId|path|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|The globally unique ID of the borrow product.|

## Sign transaction via end user EVM account

<a id="opIdsignEvmTransactionWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/sign/transaction \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
    "transaction": "0xf86b098505d21dba00830334509431415daf58e2c6b7323b4c58712fd92952145da79018080",
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/sign/transaction`

Signs a transaction with the given end user EVM account.
The transaction should be serialized as a hex string using [RLP](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/data-structures-and-encoding/rlp/).

The transaction must be an [EIP-1559 dynamic fee transaction](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-1559.md). The developer is responsible for ensuring that the unsigned transaction is valid, as the API will not validate the transaction.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
  "transaction": "0xf86b098505d21dba00830334509431415daf58e2c6b7323b4c58712fd92952145da79018080",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
}
```

<h3 id="sign-transaction-via-end-user-evm-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|X-Developer-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» address|body|string|true|The 0x-prefixed address of the EVM account belonging to the end user.|
|» transaction|body|string|true|The RLP-encoded transaction to sign, as a 0x-prefixed hex string.|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|false|Required when not using delegated signing. The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth Header.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "signedTransaction": "0x1b0c9cf8cd4554c6c6d9e7311e88f1be075d7f25b418a044f4bf2c0a42a93e212ad0a8b54de9e0b5f7e3812de3f2c6cc79aa8c3e1c02e7ad14b4a8f42012c2c01b"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "malformed_transaction",
  "errorMessage": "Malformed unsigned transaction."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "unauthorized",
  "errorMessage": "The request is not properly authenticated."
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "payment_method_required",
  "errorMessage": "A valid payment method is required to complete this operation. Please add a payment method to your account at https://portal.cdp.coinbase.com."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "forbidden",
  "errorMessage": "Unable to complete the requested signing or sending operation for this address."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "not_found",
  "errorMessage": "EVM account with the given address not found."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "already_exists",
  "errorMessage": "Another request with the same idempotency key is currently processing."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json

  "errorType": "idempotency_error",
  "errorMessage": "Idempotency key '8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324' was already used with a different request payload. Please try again with a new idempotency key."
}
```

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

```json
{
  "errorType": "bad_gateway",
  "errorMessage": "Bad gateway. Please try again later."
}
```

```json
{
  "errorType": "service_unavailable",
  "errorMessage": "Service unavailable. Please try again later."
}
```

## Send transaction via end user EVM account

<a id="opIdsendEvmTransactionWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/send/transaction \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
    "network": "base-sepolia",
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
    "transaction": "0xf86b098505d21dba00830334509431415daf58e2c6b7323b4c58712fd92952145da79018080"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/send/transaction`

Signs a transaction with the given end user EVM account and sends it to the indicated supported network. This API handles nonce management and gas estimation, leaving the developer to provide only the minimal set of fields necessary to send the transaction. The transaction should be serialized as a hex string using [RLP](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/data-structures-and-encoding/rlp/).

The transaction must be an [EIP-1559 dynamic fee transaction](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-1559.md).


**Transaction fields and API behavior**

- `to` *(Required)*: The address of the contract or account to send the transaction to.
- `chainId` *(Ignored)*: The value of the `chainId` field in the transaction is ignored.
  The transaction will be sent to the network indicated by the `network` field in the request body.

- `nonce` *(Optional)*: The nonce to use for the transaction. If not provided, the API will assign
   a nonce to the transaction based on the current state of the account.

- `maxPriorityFeePerGas` *(Optional)*: The maximum priority fee per gas to use for the transaction.
   If not provided, the API will estimate a value based on current network conditions.

- `maxFeePerGas` *(Optional)*: The maximum fee per gas to use for the transaction.
   If not provided, the API will estimate a value based on current network conditions.

- `gasLimit` *(Optional)*: The gas limit to use for the transaction. If not provided, the API will estimate a value
  based on the `to` and `data` fields of the transaction.

- `value` *(Optional)*: The amount of ETH, in wei, to send with the transaction.
- `data` *(Optional)*: The data to send with the transaction; only used for contract calls.
- `accessList` *(Optional)*: The access list to use for the transaction.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
  "network": "base-sepolia",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
  "transaction": "0xf86b098505d21dba00830334509431415daf58e2c6b7323b4c58712fd92952145da79018080"
}
```

<h3 id="send-transaction-via-end-user-evm-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|X-Developer-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» address|body|string|true|The 0x-prefixed address of the EVM account belonging to the end user.|
|» network|body|string|true|The network to send the transaction to.|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|false|Required when not using delegated signing. The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth Header.|
|» transaction|body|string|true|The RLP-encoded transaction to sign and send, as a 0x-prefixed hex string.|

|» network|base-sepolia|

## Send USDC on EVM

<a id="opIdsendEvmAssetWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e/send/usdc \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "to": "0x1234567890123456789012345678901234567890",
    "amount": "25.50",
    "network": "base-sepolia",
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/{address}/send/{asset}`

Sends USDC from an end user's EVM account (EOA or Smart Account) to a recipient address on a supported EVM network. This endpoint simplifies USDC transfers by automatically handling contract resolution, decimal conversion, gas estimation, and transaction encoding.
The `amount` field accepts human-readable amounts as decimal strings (e.g., "1.5", "25.50").

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "to": "0x1234567890123456789012345678901234567890",
  "amount": "25.50",
  "network": "base-sepolia",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
}
```

<h3 id="send-usdc-on-evm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|address|path|object|true|The 0x-prefixed address of the EVM account (EOA or Smart Account) to send USDC from. The address does not need to be checksummed.|
|asset|path|string|true|The asset to send. Currently only "usdc" is supported.|
|X-Developer-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» to|body|object|true|The 0x-prefixed address of the recipient.|
|» amount|body|string|true|The amount of USDC to send as a decimal string (e.g., "1.5" or "25.50").|
|» network|body|string|true|The EVM network to send USDC on.|
|» useCdpPaymaster|body|boolean|false|Whether to use CDP Paymaster to sponsor gas fees. Only applicable for EVM Smart Accounts. When true, the transaction gas will be paid by the Paymaster, allowing users to send USDC without holding native gas tokens. Ignored for EOA accounts. Cannot be used together with `paymasterUrl`.|
|» paymasterUrl|body|object|false|Optional custom Paymaster URL to use for gas sponsorship. Only applicable for EVM Smart Accounts. This allows you to use your own Paymaster service instead of CDP's Paymaster. Cannot be used together with `useCdpPaymaster`.|
|» paymasterContext|body|[PaymasterContext](#schemapaymastercontext)|false|The ERC-7677 `context` object forwarded to the paymaster service as part of the `paymasterService` capability. The fields in this object are defined by the paymaster service provider; CDP forwards them to the paymaster unchanged. This field is only valid when a paymaster is configured for the request. Providing `paymasterContext` without a paymaster configured results in an `invalid_request` error.|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|false|Required when not using delegated signing. The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth Header.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|asset|usdc|
|» network|base|
|» network|base-sepolia|
|» network|ethereum|
|» network|ethereum-sepolia|
|» network|avalanche|
|» network|polygon|
|» network|optimism|
|» network|arbitrum|
|» network|arbitrum-sepolia|
|» network|world|
|» network|world-sepolia|

## Sign EIP-191 message via end user EVM account

<a id="opIdsignEvmMessageWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/sign/message \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
    "message": "Hello, world!",
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/sign/message`

Signs an [EIP-191](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-191) message with the given end user EVM account.

Per the specification, the message in the request body is prepended with `0x19 <0x45 (E)> <thereum Signed Message:\n" + len(message)>` before being signed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
  "message": "Hello, world!",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|X-Developer-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» address|body|string|true|The 0x-prefixed address of the EVM account belonging to the end user.|
|» message|body|string|true|The message to sign.|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|false|Required when not using delegated signing. The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth Header.|

`GET /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/address/{address}/delegation`

## Create account-scoped delegation for end user

<a id="opIdcreateDelegationForEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/address/0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e/delegation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'X-Wallet-Auth: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOjEyMywicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIiwiZXhwIjoxNzAxOTgwMDAwfQ.HWvMTKmCCTxHaxjvZyLaC6UQ6TV3ErTDWBf7zmdH0Lw' \
  -d '{
    "expiresAt": "2026-02-03T10:35:00Z",
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/address/{address}/delegation`

Creates an account-scoped delegation that allows a developer to sign on behalf of an end user for a single blockchain account (identified by its address) for the specified duration. The end user must be authenticated to authorize this delegation.
Multiple account-scoped delegations may exist concurrently for a single end user (one per canonical account address). Account-scoped and user-scoped delegations cannot coexist for the same user.
When the address corresponds to an EVM Smart Account, the delegation is scoped to the Smart Account's owner EOA rather than the Smart Account address itself. This means `/address/{smartAccountAddress}/delegation` and `/address/{ownerEoaAddress}/delegation` resolve to the same delegation, and the 409 `account_scoped_delegation_active` error may be returned when creating via either address if one already exists for the canonical owner.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiresAt": "2026-02-03T10:35:00Z",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
}
```

<h3 id="create-account-scoped-delegation-for-end-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|true|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|address|path|[BlockchainAddress](#schemablockchainaddress)|true|The blockchain address of the end user account to scope this delegation to. Format varies by network (e.g., 0x-prefixed for EVM, base58 for Solana). For EVM addresses, matching is case-insensitive.|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expiresAt|body|string(date-time)|true|The date until which the delegation is valid.|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|true|The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth Header.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "expiresAt": "2026-02-03T10:35:00Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Field 'expiresAt' is required.",
  "errorLink": "https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/errors#invalid-request"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "unauthorized",
  "errorMessage": "The request is not properly authenticated."
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "payment_method_required",
  "errorMessage": "A valid payment method is required to complete this operation. Please add a payment method to your account at https://portal.cdp.coinbase.com."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "not_found",
  "errorMessage": "No account with the given address exists for this end user.",
  "errorLink": "https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/errors#not-found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json

  "errorType": "already_exists",
  "errorMessage": "A user-scoped delegation is already active for this user. Revoke it before creating an account-scoped delegation.",

}
```

> 422 Response

```json
}
```

## Revoke account-scoped delegation for end user

<a id="opIdrevokeDelegationForEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/address/0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e/delegation/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/address/{address}/delegation/revoke`

Revokes the active account-scoped delegation for the specified end user account. Other account-scoped delegations for the same user are unaffected. This operation can be performed by the end user themselves or by a developer using their API key.
When the address corresponds to an EVM Smart Account, this revokes the delegation for the Smart Account's owner EOA.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-account-scoped-delegation-for-end-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Developer-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|address|path|[BlockchainAddress](#schemablockchainaddress)|true|The blockchain address of the end user account whose delegation should be revoked. For EVM addresses, matching is case-insensitive.|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|[RevokeDelegationRequest](#schemarevokedelegationrequest)|true|none|

## Create EIP-7702 delegation for end user EVM account

<a id="opIdcreateEvmEip7702DelegationWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/eip7702/delegation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
    "network": "base",
    "enableSpendPermissions": true,
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/eip7702/delegation`

Creates an EIP-7702 delegation for an end user's EVM EOA account, upgrading it with smart account capabilities.

This endpoint:
- Retrieves delegation artifacts from onchain
- Signs the EIP-7702 authorization for delegation
- Assembles and submits a Type 4 transaction
- Creates an associated smart account object

The delegation allows the EVM EOA to be used as a smart account, which enables batched transactions and gas sponsorship via paymaster.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
  "network": "base",
  "enableSpendPermissions": true,
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2"
}
```

<h3 id="create-eip-7702-delegation-for-end-user-evm-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|X-Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|An optional string request header for making requests safely retryable.<br>When included, duplicate requests with the same key will return identical responses.<br>Refer to our [Idempotency docs](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/idempotency) for more information on using idempotency keys.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|X-Developer-Auth|header|string|false|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» address|body|string|true|The 0x-prefixed address of the EVM account to delegate.|
|» network|body|[EvmEip7702DelegationNetwork](#schemaevmeip7702delegationnetwork)|true|The network for the EIP-7702 delegation.|
|» enableSpendPermissions|body|boolean|false|Whether to configure spend permissions for the upgraded, delegated account. When enabled, the account can grant permissions for third parties to spend on its behalf.|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|false|Required when not using delegated signing. The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth Header.|

## List borrow positions for an end user smart account

<a id="opIdlistBorrowPositionsWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/smart-accounts/0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e/borrow-positions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/smart-accounts/{address}/borrow-positions`

Lists the borrow positions held by an end user smart account, with the live onchain state of each position read at a point-in-time snapshot.
A borrow position represents collateral posted and a loan borrowed against it in a borrow product, such as a Morpho Blue market that lends USDC against cbBTC. Each position reports its current collateral and debt balances, its health factor, and its health status. Returns an empty list if the smart account has no borrow positions.

<h3 id="list-borrow-positions-for-an-end-user-smart-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|address|path|string|true|The address of the EVM Smart Account to list borrow positions for.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return per page.|
|pageToken|query|string|false|The token for the next page of resources, if any.|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|

## Create a borrow position for an end user smart account

<a id="opIdcreateBorrowPositionWithEndUserAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2/evm/smart-accounts/0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e/borrow-positions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'X-Wallet-Auth: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOjEyMywicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIiwiZXhwIjoxNzAxOTgwMDAwfQ.HWvMTKmCCTxHaxjvZyLaC6UQ6TV3ErTDWBf7zmdH0Lw' \
  -d '{
    "borrowProductId": "bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df",
    "collateralAmount": "1",
    "loanAmount": "100",
    "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
    "useCdpPaymaster": false,
    "paymasterUrl": "https://api.developer.coinbase.com/rpc/v1/base/AbCdEf123456"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/embedded-wallet-api/end-users/{userId}/evm/smart-accounts/{address}/borrow-positions`

Creates a borrow position for a specific borrow product, by posting collateral from an end user smart account and borrowing a loan against it. One position can be opened per borrow product for a given smart account.
A borrow product is a protocol-native representation of a borrowable market, such as a Morpho Blue market that lends USDC against cbBTC. The `borrowProductId` identifies the product to borrow against, and the `collateralAmount` and `loanAmount` specify the collateral to post and the loan to take, both expressed as decimal strings in standard unit denomination of their respective tokens.
A user operation is broadcast to open the position onchain. Poll `getUserOperationWithEndUserAccount` with the returned `userOpHash` until it reaches a terminal state. Once the user operation succeeds onchain, use the borrow positions list endpoint to view the user's active positions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "borrowProductId": "bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df",
  "collateralAmount": "1",
  "loanAmount": "100",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
  "useCdpPaymaster": false,
  "paymasterUrl": "https://api.developer.coinbase.com/rpc/v1/base/AbCdEf123456"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-borrow-position-for-an-end-user-smart-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Wallet-Auth|header|string|true|A JWT signed using your Wallet Secret, encoded in base64. Refer to the<br>[Generate Wallet Token](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/v2/authentication#2-generate-wallet-token)<br>section of our Authentication docs for more details on how to generate your Wallet Token.<br>|
|userId|path|string|true|The ID of the end user.|
|address|path|string|true|The address of the EVM Smart Account to open the borrow position from.|
|projectID|query|string|false|The ID of the CDP Project. Required for end users authenticated using custom auth (i.e. a non-CDP JWT provider).|
|body|body|[CreateBorrowPositionRequest](#schemacreateborrowpositionrequest)|true|none|
|» borrowProductId|body|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|The globally unique ID of the borrow product, which is a UUID prefixed with the string `bp_`.|
|» collateralAmount|body|object|true|The amount of collateral to post, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the collateral token (i.e. "1" for 1 cbBTC).|
|» loanAmount|body|object|true|The amount of the loan token to borrow, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the loan token (i.e. "100" for 100 USDC).|
|» walletSecretId|body|string|true|The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth header.|
|» useCdpPaymaster|body|boolean|true|Whether to use the CDP Paymaster for the user operation. When `true`, `paymasterUrl` must not be set.|
|» paymasterUrl|body|object|false|Paymaster URL to use for the user operation. Must not be set when `useCdpPaymaster` is `true`.<br>If `useCdpPaymaster` is `false` and no `paymasterUrl` is set, the smart account must have sufficient funds to cover network fees.|
|» paymasterContext|body|object|false|Optional paymaster metadata forwarded to the configured paymaster service. Valid only when a paymaster is configured via `useCdpPaymaster: true` or a `paymasterUrl`.|
