## Create webhook subscription

<a id="opIdcreateWebhookSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/data/webhooks/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Liquidity pool burn events.",
    "eventTypes": [
      "onchain.activity.detected"
    ],
    "labels": {
      "network": "base-mainnet",
      "contract_address": "0xcd1f9777571493aeacb7eae45cd30a226d3e612d",
      "event_name": "Burn"
    },
    "target": {
      "url": "https://api.example.com/webhooks"
    },
    "isEnabled": true
  }'
```

`POST /v2/data/webhooks/subscriptions`

Subscribe to real-time events across CDP products. A webhook subscription provides a `targetURL` and other relevant endpoint configuration to enable receiving webhooks when events occur.

An entity can have up to 100 webhook subscriptions. Once this limit is reached, new webhook subscription creation requests return a `400` error with `errorType: subscription_limit_exceeded`.

### Webhook Signature Verification

All webhooks include an HMAC-SHA256 signed header for security. The signature is signed with the secret that is returned in the `secret` field when creating a subscription.

Do not lose the secret, as you will not be able to recreate it. If you lose the secret, you will need to create a new subscription.

See the [verification guide](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/onramp-&-offramp/webhooks#webhook-signature-verification) for implementation details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Liquidity pool burn events.",
  "eventTypes": [
    "onchain.activity.detected"
  ],
  "labels": {
    "network": "base-mainnet",
    "contract_address": "0xcd1f9777571493aeacb7eae45cd30a226d3e612d",
    "event_name": "Burn"
  },
  "target": {
    "url": "https://api.example.com/webhooks"
  },
  "isEnabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-webhook-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WebhookSubscriptionRequest](#schemawebhooksubscriptionrequest)|true|none|
|» description|body|[WebhookDescription](#schemawebhookdescription)|false|A human-readable description of the webhook subscription.<br>Must be at most 100 characters.<br>|
|» eventTypes|body|[[EventType](#schemaeventtype)]|true|Types of events to subscribe to. Event types follow a dot-separated format:<br>service.resource.verb (e.g., "onchain.activity.detected", "wallet.activity.detected", "onramp.transaction.created",<br>"acceptance.payment_session.authorization_succeeded").<br>The subscription will only receive events matching these types AND the label filter(s).<br>|
|» isEnabled|body|boolean|true|Whether the subscription is enabled.|
|» target|body|[WebhookTarget](#schemawebhooktarget)|true|Target configuration for webhook delivery.<br>Specifies the destination URL and any custom headers to include in webhook requests.<br>|
|» metadata|body|[WebhookMetadata](#schemawebhookmetadata)|false|Optional subscription metadata. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values must each contain between 1 and 50 characters.|
|» labels|body|[WebhookRequestLabels](#schemawebhookrequestlabels)|false|String-valued filters supplied when creating or updating a webhook subscription.<br>The subscription's `eventTypes` determine whether labels are required and which<br>label keys are accepted. A subscription accepts at most 20 client-supplied labels.<br><br>#### Label Behavior<br><br>An event must match ALL labels to fire to your subscription `targetURL`. When multiple labels are supplied, the event must match ALL labels to fire to your subscription `targetURL`.<br>|

event types, target URL, filtering criteria, and enabled status.
All required fields must be provided, even if they are not being changed.

- Change target URL or headers
- Add/remove event type filters
- Update multi-label filtering criteria
- Enable/disable subscription

```json
  }
}
```

`DELETE /v2/data/webhooks/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`

Permanently delete a webhook subscription and stop all event deliveries.
This action cannot be undone.

### Important Notes
- All webhook deliveries will cease immediately
- Subscription cannot be recovered after deletion
- Consider disabling instead of deleting for temporary pauses

## List webhook subscription events

<a id="opIdlistWebhookSubscriptionEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/data/webhooks/subscriptions/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/data/webhooks/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/events`

Retrieve webhook event delivery attempts for a specific subscription.
Returns event deliveries in descending order by creation time (newest first),
including delivery status, retry count, and response details.

### Use Cases
- Debug webhook delivery failures and inspect response codes
- Monitor delivery status and retry counts
- Audit event delivery history for a subscription
- Verify that expected events were sent to webhook URLs

### Filtering
Use optional query parameters to narrow results:
- `eventId` — find a specific event by ID
- `minCreatedAt` / `maxCreatedAt` — filter by time range
- `eventTypeNames` — filter by event type (comma-separated)

**Note:** Results are limited to the 50 most recent events (newest first). No pagination is supported.


<h3 id="list-webhook-subscription-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier for the webhook subscription.|
|eventId|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by a specific event ID.|
|minCreatedAt|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter events created at or after this timestamp (RFC 3339 format).|
|maxCreatedAt|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter events created at or before this timestamp (RFC 3339 format).|
|eventTypeNames|query|string|false|Filter by event type names (comma-separated).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "eventId": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
      "eventTypeName": "onchain.activity.detected",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "succeededAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:02Z",
      "retryCount": 0,

        "elapsedTimeMs": 142,
        "body": "ok"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-x402-facilitator">x402 Facilitator</h1>

The x402 payment protocol is an HTTP-based payment protocol that enables developers running resource servers to accept payments from users using a variety of payment methods.
For more details on the x402 payment protocol, please see the [x402 specification](https://www.x402.org/).
The x402 Facilitator APIs enable you to facilitate payments using the x402 payment protocol by exposing two APIs:
- `POST /v2/x402/verify`: Verify a payment with a supported scheme and network.
- `POST /v2/x402/settle`: Settle a payment with a supported scheme and network.

## Verify payment

<a id="opIdverifyX402Payment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "x402Version": 2,
    "paymentPayload": {
      "x402Version": 2,
      "accepted": {
        "scheme": "exact",
        "network": "eip155:84532",
        "asset": "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e",
        "amount": "1000",
        "payTo": "0x122F8Fcaf2152420445Aa424E1D8C0306935B5c9",
        "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60,
        "extra": {
          "name": "USDC",
          "version": "2"
        }
      },
      "payload": {
        "signature": "0xf3746613c2d920b5fdabc0856f2aeb2d4f88ee6037b8cc5d04a71a4462f134801234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1b",
        "authorization": {
          "from": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
          "to": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
          "value": "1000000000000000000",
          "validAfter": "1716150000",
          "validBefore": "1716150000",
          "nonce": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef"
        }
      },
      "resource": {
        "url": "https://api.example.com/premium/resource/123",
        "description": "Premium API access for data analysis.",
        "mimeType": "application/json"
      }
    },
    "paymentRequirements": {
      "scheme": "exact",
      "network": "eip155:8453",
      "asset": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
      "amount": "1000000",
      "payTo": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
      "maxTimeoutSeconds": 10,
      "extra": {
        "name": "USDC",
        "version": "2"
      }
    }
  }'
```

<h3 id="verify-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» x402Version|body|[X402Version](#schemax402version)|true|The version of the x402 protocol.|
|» paymentPayload|body|[x402PaymentPayload](#schemax402paymentpayload)|true|The x402 protocol payment payload that the client attaches to x402-paid API requests to the resource server in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header.<br>For EVM networks, smart account signatures can be longer than 65 bytes.|
|» paymentRequirements|body|[x402PaymentRequirements](#schemax402paymentrequirements)|true|The x402 protocol payment requirements that the resource server expects the client's payment payload to meet.|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|isValid|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the payment is valid.|
|invalidReason|[x402VerifyInvalidReason](#schemax402verifyinvalidreason)|false|none|The reason the payment is invalid on the x402 protocol.|
|invalidMessage|string|false|none|The message describing the invalid reason.|
|payer|object|true|none|The onchain address of the client that is paying for the resource.<br><br>For EVM networks, the payer will be a 0x-prefixed, checksum EVM address.<br><br>For Solana-based networks, the payer will be a base58-encoded Solana address.|
|extra|object|false|none|Optional scheme-specific verify metadata returned by the facilitator.|

## Settle payment

<a id="opIdsettleX402Payment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/settle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "x402Version": 2,
    "paymentPayload": {
      "x402Version": 2,
      "accepted": {
```

`POST /v2/x402/settle`

Settle an x402 protocol payment with a specific scheme and network.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "paymentPayload": {
    "x402Version": 2,
    "accepted": {
      "scheme": "exact",
      "network": "eip155:84532",
      "asset": "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e",
      "amount": "1000",
      "payTo": "0x122F8Fcaf2152420445Aa424E1D8C0306935B5c9",
      "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60,
      "extra": {
        "name": "USDC",
        "version": "2"
      }
    },
    "payload": {
      "signature": "0xf3746613c2d920b5fdabc0856f2aeb2d4f88ee6037b8cc5d04a71a4462f134801234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1b",
      "authorization": {
        "from": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
        "to": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
        "value": "1000000000000000000",
        "validAfter": "1716150000",
        "validBefore": "1716150000",
        "nonce": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef"
      }
    },
    "resource": {
      "url": "https://api.example.com/premium/resource/123",
      "description": "Premium API access for data analysis.",
      "mimeType": "application/json"
    }
  },
  "paymentRequirements": {
    "scheme": "exact",
    "network": "eip155:8453",
    "asset": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",

    "payTo": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",

    }

}
```

<h3 id="settle-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» x402Version|body|[X402Version](#schemax402version)|true|The version of the x402 protocol.|
|» paymentPayload|body|[x402PaymentPayload](#schemax402paymentpayload)|true|The x402 protocol payment payload that the client attaches to x402-paid API requests to the resource server in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header.<br>For EVM networks, smart account signatures can be longer than 65 bytes.|
|» paymentRequirements|body|[x402PaymentRequirements](#schemax402paymentrequirements)|true|The x402 protocol payment requirements that the resource server expects the client's payment payload to meet.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» x402Version|1|
|» x402Version|2|

<h3 id="settle-payment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successfully settled payment on the x402 protocol.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Unsuccessful payment settlement on the x402 protocol.|[x402SettlePaymentRejection](#schemax402settlepaymentrejection)|
|402|Payment Required|A payment method is required to complete this operation.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|502|Bad Gateway|Bad gateway.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="settle-payment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|success|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the payment settlement is successful.|
|errorReason|[x402SettleErrorReason](#schemax402settleerrorreason)|false|none|The reason the payment settlement errored on the x402 protocol.|
|errorMessage|string|false|none|The message describing the error reason.|
|payer|object|true|none|The onchain address of the client that is paying for the resource.<br><br>For EVM networks, the payer will be a 0x-prefixed, checksum EVM address.<br><br>For Solana-based networks, the payer will be a base58-encoded Solana address.|
|transaction|string|true|none|The transaction of the settlement.<br>For EVM networks, the transaction will be a 0x-prefixed, EVM transaction hash.<br>For Solana-based networks, the transaction will be a base58-encoded Solana signature.|
|network|string|true|none|The network where the settlement occurred.|
|amount|string|false|none|The amount that was settled, in atomic units.|
|extra|object|false|none|Optional scheme-specific success metadata returned by the facilitator.|

## Get supported payment schemes and networks

<a id="opIdsupportedX402PaymentKinds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/supported \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## List x402 resources

<a id="opIdlistX402DiscoveryResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/resources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/x402/discovery/resources`

Lists all active discovered x402 resources.
This endpoint returns resources that have been discovered and cached by the x402 facilitator, including their payment requirements and metadata.
The response is paginated, and by default, returns 100 items per page.

<h3 id="list-x402-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|query|string|false|Filter by protocol type (e.g., "http", "mcp").<br>Currently, the only supported protocol type is "http".|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of discovered x402 resources to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset of the first discovered x402 resource to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "items": [
    {
      "resource": "https://api.example.com/weather/forecast",
      "description": "Real-time weather forecast data.",
      "type": "http",
      "x402Version": 2,
      "lastUpdated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "accepts": [
        {
          "scheme": "exact",
          "network": "eip155:8453",

          "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60
        }
      ],
      "extensions": {
        "bazaar": {
          "info": {
            "input": {
              "type": "http",
              "method": "GET"
            }
          },
          "schema": {}
        }
      },
      "quality": {
        "l30DaysTotalCalls": 42,
        "l30DaysUniquePayers": 15,
        "lastCalledAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
      },

    "limit": 100,
    "offset": 0,

  }
}
```

## List merchant discovery info

<a id="opIdlistX402DiscoveryMerchant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/merchant?payTo=0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/x402/discovery/merchant`

Gets x402 merchant discovery information for a given merchant payment address.
This endpoint returns all active x402 resources associated with the specified `payTo` address, allowing clients to discover what payment-gated resources a merchant exposes and their corresponding payment requirements.
If no active resources are found for the `payTo` address, the endpoint returns an empty `resources` list.
The response is paginated, and by default, returns 20 items per page.

<h3 id="list-merchant-discovery-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payTo|query|[BlockchainAddress](#schemablockchainaddress)|true|The merchant's payment address to look up.<br>This is the onchain address that payment requirements route funds to.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset of the first resource to return.|

> Example responses

## Search x402 resources

<a id="opIdsearchX402Resources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/x402/discovery/search`

Searches for active x402 resources using a text query and optional filters.
Supports both text-based and vector-based search depending on availability. Results are sorted by relevance and quality score.
Legacy network names (e.g., `base`, `base-sepolia`, `solana`) are automatically normalized to their CAIP-2 equivalents.
The response is limited to 20 items per request. If more results exist, `partialResults` will be `true`.

<h3 id="search-x402-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Full-text or semantic search query to find matching resources.|
|network|query|string|false|Filter results by network in CAIP-2 format (e.g., `eip155:8453`) or legacy name (e.g., `base`, `base-sepolia`, `solana`).<br>Legacy names are normalized to their CAIP-2 equivalents before filtering.|
|asset|query|string|false|Filter results by asset address.<br>For EVM networks, provide a 0x-prefixed EVM address. For Solana networks, provide a base58-encoded address.<br>Matching is case-insensitive.|
|scheme|query|string|false|Filter results by payment scheme (e.g., `exact`).|
|payTo|query|[BlockchainAddress](#schemablockchainaddress)|false|Filter results by the merchant's payment address.<br>For EVM networks, provide a 0x-prefixed EVM address. For Solana networks, provide a base58-encoded address.|
|urlSubstring|query|string|false|Filter results to resources whose URL contains this value (case-insensitive substring match against the resource URL).<br>Useful for narrowing results to a specific domain, subdomain, or path segment. Combine with `query` to perform semantic search restricted to a URL subset.<br>Tip: include enough of the URL to disambiguate (e.g. `api.example.com` rather than `example`) — a short substring may also match resources whose path contains the same string.|
|maxUsdPrice|query|string|false|Filter results to resources with a USD price at or below this value.|
|extensions|query|[string]|false|Filter results to resources that support the specified protocol extensions. Can be specified multiple times to filter by multiple extensions.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|Filter results to resources published with any of the specified provider tags (case-sensitive exact match). Can be specified multiple times to filter by multiple tags; a resource matches if it carries at least one of the supplied tags (OR).|
|bundleSlugs|query|[string]|false|Filter results to resources that belong to any of the specified curated bundles (by bundle slug). Can be specified multiple times to filter by multiple bundles; a resource matches if it belongs to at least one of the supplied bundles (OR).|
|curatedOnly|query|boolean|false|When `true`, restrict results to Coinbase-curated resources (those with `curated: true`). When `false` or omitted, both curated and non-curated resources are returned.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of resources to return. Must be a positive integer no greater than 20.<br>Defaults to 20.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "resources": [
    {
      "resource": "https://api.example.com/weather/forecast",
      "description": "Real-time weather forecast data.",
      "type": "http",
      "x402Version": 2,
      "lastUpdated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "extensions": {
        "bazaar": {
          "info": {
            "input": {
              "type": "http",
              "method": "GET"
            }
          },
          "schema": {}
        }
      },
      "accepts": [
        {
          "scheme": "exact",
          "network": "eip155:8453",
          "amount": "1000000",
          "payTo": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
          "asset": "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e",
          "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60
        }
      ],
      "quality": {
        "l30DaysTotalCalls": 42,
        "l30DaysUniquePayers": 15,
        "lastCalledAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
      },
      "curated": true,
      "skillUrl": "https://skills.cdp.coinbase.com/weather-api/SKILL.md"
    }
  ],
  "partialResults": false,
  "searchMethod": "text"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "limit must be a positive integer."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

> 502 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "bad_gateway",
  "errorMessage": "Bad gateway. Please try again later."
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "service_unavailable",
  "errorMessage": "Service unavailable. Please try again later."
}
```

|200|OK|Successfully retrieved matching x402 resources.|[x402SearchResourcesResponse](#schemax402searchresourcesresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request parameters.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

## Handle MCP JSON-RPC request

<a id="opIdpostX402DiscoveryMcp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/mcp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "tools/list",
    "params": {}
  }'
```

`POST /v2/x402/discovery/mcp`

Handles JSON-RPC requests for the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Supports MCP methods for discovering x402 payment resources and tools.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/list",
  "params": {}
}
```

<h3 id="handle-mcp-json-rpc-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[x402McpRequest](#schemax402mcprequest)|true|none|
|» jsonrpc|body|string|true|JSON-RPC version, must be "2.0".|
|» id|body|string \| integer|false|Request identifier.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» method|body|string|true|The MCP method to invoke.|
|» params|body|object|false|Optional parameters for the method.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» jsonrpc|2.0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "tools": []
  },
  "error": {
    "code": -32600,
    "message": "Invalid Request",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Invalid JSON-RPC request. Please check the request format."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

`GET /v2/x402/discovery/bundles`

Lists the available curated x402 workflow bundles. A bundle is an ordered, named grouping of curated x402 resources that together cover a common agent workflow.

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/x402/discovery/bundles/{bundleSlug}`

<h3 id="get-an-x402-bundle-parameters">Parameters</h3>

</aside>

## Validate x402 endpoint

<a id="opIdvalidateX402Resource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "resource": "https://api.example.com/weather/forecast",
    "method": "GET"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/x402/validate`

Validates an x402 endpoint's bazaar-discovery configuration by probing the seller's URL live.
Returns a uniform array of preflight check results (reachable, returns402, hasBazaarExtension, parse) and a simulated facilitator accept/reject decision so sellers and agents can confirm their endpoint is ready to be discovered before going live.
This operation is read-only: it performs no payment and does not index the resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resource": "https://api.example.com/weather/forecast",
  "method": "GET"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-x402-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[x402ValidateRequest](#schemax402validaterequest)|true|none|
|» resource|body|object|true|HTTPS URL of the x402 endpoint to validate. Must use the `https://` scheme.|
|» method|body|string|false|The HTTP method used to probe the endpoint. Only GET and POST are supported; other verbs are intentionally rejected because x402 resources are expected to respond to these methods.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» method|GET|
|» method|POST|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "statusCode": 402,
  "x402Version": 2,
  "preflight": [
    {
      "check": "reachable",
      "passed": true,
      "detail": "Endpoint responded within the timeout.",
      "severity": "required"
    },
    {
      "check": "returns_402",
      "passed": true,
      "detail": "Endpoint responded with HTTP 402 Payment Required.",
      "expected": "402",
      "actual": "402",
      "severity": "required"
    },
    {
      "check": "has_bazaar_extension",
      "passed": true,
      "detail": "Payment requirements include the bazaar discovery extension.",
      "severity": "required"
    },
    {
      "check": "parse",
      "passed": true,
      "detail": "Payment requirements parsed successfully.",
      "severity": "required"
    }
  ],
  "paymentRequirements": {
    "scheme": "exact",
    "network": "base",
    "maxAmountRequired": "100000",
    "resource": "https://api.example.com/weather/forecast",
    "description": "Real-time weather forecast data.",
    "mimeType": "application/json",
    "payTo": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
    "asset": "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e",
    "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60
  },
  "bazaarExtension": {
    "info": {
      "input": {
        "type": "http",
        "method": "GET"
      }
    },
    "schema": {}
  },
  "simulation": {
    "outcome": "accepted"
  },
  "index": {
    "active": true,
    "lastCrawledAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00Z",
    "quality": {
      "l30DaysTotalCalls": 42,
      "l30DaysUniquePayers": 15,
      "lastCalledAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00Z"
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "invalid_request",
  "errorMessage": "Invalid request. resource is required and must be a valid HTTPS URL."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "internal_server_error",
  "errorMessage": "An internal server error occurred. Please try again later."
}
```

> 502 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "bad_gateway",
  "errorMessage": "Bad gateway. Please try again later."
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "errorType": "service_unavailable",
  "errorMessage": "Service unavailable. Please try again later."
}
```

<h1 id="coinbase-developer-platform-apis-webhooks-1">Webhooks</h1>

## Onchain activity detected

<a id="opIdonchainActivityDetectedWebhook"></a>

`POST onchainActivityDetected`

Triggered when onchain activity matching your subscription filters is detected. Your API will receive a POST request at the webhook URL you configured. Use `labels` on your webhook subscription to filter which onchain events are delivered (see the Create Webhook Subscription endpoint for allowed labels).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "block_number": 46218191,
  "contract_address": "0x940181a94A35A4569E4529A3CDfB74e38FD98631",
  "event_name": "Transfer",
  "event_signature": "Transfer(address,address,uint256)",
  "log_index": 29,
  "network": "base-mainnet",
  "parameters": {
    "from": "0xF33a96b5932D9E9B9A0eDA447AbD8C9d48d2e0c8",
    "to": "0x61040E143A77F165Ba44543AF4A079F2C809D14b",
    "value": "474891138228179365"
  },
  "timestamp": "2026-05-19T21:22:10Z",
  "transaction_from": "0x3E16D476D8Df15e3E776EAa5A46f37EC44C830cD",
  "transaction_hash": "0xa58e4471bcce875b1ea49cc0864a620d3a484b9b7c1b0b4fd18ce83f5b30e5e0",
  "transaction_to": "0x61040E143A77F165Ba44543AF4A079F2C809D14b"
}
```

<h3 id="onchain-activity-detected-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OnchainActivityDetectedEvent](#schemaonchainactivitydetectedevent)|true|The decoded blockchain event data. Payload shape varies by the type of onchain activity detected (token transfer, contract interaction, etc.).|
|» block_number|body|integer(int64)|true|The block number containing the transaction that emitted the event.|
|» contract_address|body|string|true|The contract address that emitted the event.|
|» event_name|body|string|true|The name of the decoded contract event.|
|» event_signature|body|string|true|The canonical event signature used to decode the log, including parameter types (e.g., `Transfer(address,address,uint256)`).|
|» log_index|body|integer(int64)|true|The zero-based index of the log within the transaction.|
|» network|body|string|true|The blockchain network where the activity was detected.|
|» parameters|body|[OnchainActivityEventParameters](#schemaonchainactivityeventparameters)|true|Decoded event parameters from the contract event. Keys correspond to the named arguments in the event signature (e.g., `from`, `to`, `value` for an ERC-20 `Transfer`). Values are returned as strings to preserve precision for large integers and to avoid loss for address types. The exact set of keys depends on the contract event.|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|true|The block timestamp of the transaction (ISO 8601 format).|
|» transaction_from|body|string|true|The address that initiated the transaction (the transaction sender).|
|» transaction_hash|body|string|true|The hash of the transaction that emitted the event.|
|» transaction_to|body|string|true|The address the transaction was sent to (typically a contract address).|

<h3 id="onchain-activity-detected-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Webhook received and processed successfully. Return a 200 status code to acknowledge receipt. If your endpoint does not return a 2xx status code, the webhook will be retried with exponential backoff.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Invalid signature. The webhook signature verification failed.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
webhookSignature
</aside>

```json
{
  "eventType": "acceptance.payment_session.created",
  "eventId": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "timestamp": "2025-06-15T12:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "paymentSession": {
      "paymentSessionId": "paymentSession_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
      "entityId": "entity_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
      "amount": "1.00",
      "asset": "usdc",
      "target": {
        "address": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
        "network": "base"
      },
      "autoCapture": false,
      "expiries": {
        "authorizationExpiresAt": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
        "captureExpiresAt": "2026-01-15T23:59:59.000Z",
        "refundExpiresAt": "2026-02-15T23:59:59.000Z"
      },
      "status": "created",
      "balances": {
        "capturable": "0",
        "captured": "0",
        "refundable": "0",
        "refunded": "0"
      },
      "externalReferenceId": "merchant-order-abc123",
      "metadata": {
        "customer_id": "cust_12345",
        "order_reference": "order-67890"
      },
      "createdAt": "2025-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2025-06-15T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="payment-session-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[AcceptancePaymentSessionCreatedEvent](#schemaacceptancepaymentsessioncreatedevent)|true|The `acceptance.payment_session.created` webhook event payload.|
|» eventId|body|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier for this webhook event. Use this for idempotency.|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|true|When this event occurred (ISO 8601 format).|
|» data|body|[PaymentSessionEventData](#schemapaymentsessioneventdata)|true|The data payload for a payment session webhook event. Always contains the `paymentSession` summary reflecting the session's current state. When the event was triggered by an action (authorization, capture, void, or refund), the corresponding optional field is present with the action details. For session-level events (created, canceled) no action field is included — the `paymentSession.status` value is sufficient.|
|» eventType|body|string|true|The type of webhook event.|

## Mandate created

<a id="opIdacceptanceMandateCreatedWebhook"></a>

`POST acceptanceMandateCreated`

Triggered when a mandate is created and enters `created` status. It is not yet usable; the customer must complete approval before it can be debited.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eventId": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "timestamp": "2025-06-15T12:00:00Z",
  "eventType": "acceptance.mandate.created",
  "data": {
    "mandate": {
      "mandateId": "mandate_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
      "asset": "usdc",
      "policy": {
        "maxPerAuthorization": "50.00",
        "maxPerPeriod": {
          "amount": "500.00",
          "period": "month"
        }
      },
      "status": "created",
      "expiresAt": "2027-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "url": "https://payments.coinbase.com/mandates/mandate_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
      "createdAt": "2025-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2025-06-15T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="mandate-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AcceptanceMandateCreatedEvent](#schemaacceptancemandatecreatedevent)|true|The `acceptance.mandate.created` webhook event payload.|
|» eventId|body|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier for this webhook event. Use this for idempotency.|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|true|When this event occurred (ISO 8601 format).|
|» data|body|[MandateEventData](#schemamandateeventdata)|true|The `data` payload for every mandate webhook event. Always contains the full `mandate`. Action events also carry the relevant sub-resource: `approval` on the three `approval_*` events, `revocation` on the three `revocation_*` events. The `created` and `canceled` events carry only the `mandate`.<br><br>`mandate.status` reflects only the latest action. Read `mandate.canceledAt` and `mandate.revokedAt` to know what has durably happened: the on-chain spending allowance is gone precisely when `revokedAt` is set, and canceling alone does not remove it.|

## Mandate canceled

<a id="opIdacceptanceMandateCanceledWebhook"></a>

`POST acceptanceMandateCanceled`

```json
        "network": "base",
        "asset": "usdc"

      "policy": {
        "maxPerAuthorization": "50.00",
        "maxPerPeriod": {
          "amount": "500.00",
          "period": "month"
        }
      },
      "status": "canceled",
      "expiresAt": "2027-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "revocationUrl": "https://payments.coinbase.com/mandates/mandate_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad/revoke",
      "approvedAt": "2025-06-15T12:05:00.000Z",

      "updatedAt": "2026-08-21T14:02:00.000Z"
    }

}
```

## Top-Up Link created

<a id="opIdacceptanceTopUpLinkCreatedWebhook"></a>

`POST acceptanceTopUpLinkCreated`

Triggered when the `acceptance.top_up_link.created` webhook event is emitted. Your API will receive a POST request at the webhook URL you configured. `data.topUpLink` carries the complete immutable Top-Up Link resource as created. The link expires 24 hours after creation, funds a single purchase, and is not bound to a specific payer. `data.topUpLink.customerDisplay.merchantName` contains the resolved name stored at creation, including the entity's profile-name fallback. `orderTotalAmount` and `redirectUrl` are omitted when they were not supplied at creation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eventType": "acceptance.top_up_link.created",
  "eventId": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-11T20:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "topUpLink": {
      "topUpLinkId": "topUpLink_6f2e9b41-c0f4-4bf8-a4b2-c105f9453a24",
      "topUpAmount": "100.00",
      "asset": "usdc",
      "orderTotalAmount": "130.45",
      "redirectUrl": "https://www.example-merchant.com/checkout/return?orderId=701-3358192-4471016&sig=8a3f",
      "customerDisplay": {
        "merchantName": "Example Merchant"
      },
      "topUpUrl": "https://pay.coinbase.com/top-up/topUpLink_6f2e9b41-c0f4-4bf8-a4b2-c105f9453a24",
      "expiresAt": "2026-09-12T20:00:00Z",
      "createdAt": "2026-09-11T20:00:00Z"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="top-up-link-created-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AcceptanceTopUpLinkCreatedEvent](#schemaacceptancetopuplinkcreatedevent)|true|The `acceptance.top_up_link.created` webhook event payload.|
|» eventId|body|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier for this webhook event. Use this for idempotency.|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|true|When this event occurred (ISO 8601 format).|
|» eventType|body|string|true|The type of webhook event.|
|» data|body|[TopUpLinkCreatedEventData](#schematopuplinkcreatedeventdata)|true|The `data` payload for the `acceptance.top_up_link.created` event. Carries the complete immutable `topUpLink` resource as created, including the resolved `customerDisplay.merchantName`. `orderTotalAmount` and `redirectUrl` are omitted when they were not supplied at creation.|

#### Enumerated Values

## Top-Up Link funds added

<a id="opIdacceptanceTopUpLinkFundsAddedWebhook"></a>

`POST acceptanceTopUpLinkFundsAdded`

Triggered when the `acceptance.top_up_link.funds_added` webhook event is emitted. Your API will receive a POST request at the webhook URL you configured. The event reports the purchase that spent the link. Because a link funds a single purchase, it produces at most one funds-added event; deliveries can repeat, so deduplicate on `eventId`. `toppedUpAmount` is the actual net amount credited by that purchase, denominated in `asset`; it is never cumulative and independent of the link's suggested amounts.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eventType": "acceptance.top_up_link.funds_added",
  "eventId": "223e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174001",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-11T20:08:42Z",
  "data": {
    "topUpLinkId": "topUpLink_6f2e9b41-c0f4-4bf8-a4b2-c105f9453a24",
    "toppedUpAmount": "100.00",
    "asset": "usdc"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="top-up-link-funds-added-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AcceptanceTopUpLinkFundsAddedEvent](#schemaacceptancetopuplinkfundsaddedevent)|true|The `acceptance.top_up_link.funds_added` webhook event payload.|
|» eventId|body|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier for this webhook event. Use this for idempotency.|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|true|When this event occurred (ISO 8601 format).|
|» eventType|body|string|true|The type of webhook event.|
|» data|body|[TopUpLinkFundsAddedEventData](#schematopuplinkfundsaddedeventdata)|true|The `data` payload for the `acceptance.top_up_link.funds_added` event. The event reports the purchase that spent the link. `eventId` (from `TopUpLinkEventBase`) uniquely identifies and deduplicates this event; `topUpLinkId` associates it with the link the purchase spent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» eventType|acceptance.top_up_link.funds_added|

## Customers requirement changed

<a id="opIdcustomersRequirementChangedWebhook"></a>

`POST customersRequirementChanged`

Triggered when the `customers.requirement.changed` webhook event is emitted. Your API will receive a POST request at the webhook URL you configured.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eventId": "3a7f8b2e-1c4d-4e9a-b5f6-d8a2c0e7f194",
  "eventType": "customers.requirement.changed",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-01T12:00:02Z",
  "data": {
    "customerId": "customer_38d54acb-0868-431c-a88e-1ffcb62655eb",
    "requirements": [
      {
        "field": "fullSsn",
        "status": "rejected",
        "impact": [
          "tradeCrypto"
        ]
      },
      {
        "field": "ssnLast4",
        "status": "cleared"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="customers-requirement-changed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CustomersRequirementChangedEvent](#schemacustomersrequirementchangedevent)|true|The `customers.requirement.changed` webhook event payload.|
|» eventId|body|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier for this logical webhook event. Webhooks are delivered at least once, so your endpoint may receive duplicate deliveries for the same event. Use this `eventId` as the idempotency/deduplication key.|
|» eventType|body|string|true|The type of webhook event.|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|true|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the underlying state change occurred, not the time at which this webhook was delivered.|
|» eventType|body|string|true|The type of webhook event.|
|» data|body|object|true|Payload body for the `customers.requirement.changed` event. Emitted when the status of one or more requirements changes. Several requirements may change in a single event, with each change represented by a distinct entry in the `requirements` array.|
|» » customerId|body|object|true|The CDP Customer ID the event applies to.|
|» » requirements|body|[object]|true|The set of requirements whose status changed in this event.|
|» » » field|body|object|true|The requirement that changed. Identical to the corresponding key of `requirements` on `GET /v2/customers/{customerId}`.|
|» » » status|body|string|true|The new status of the requirement after the change. `due`, `past_due`, `pending`, and `rejected` match `RequirementStatus`. `cleared` means verification passed and the requirement no longer appears on `GET /v2/customers/{customerId}`. When `status` is `rejected`, resubmit that field on the Customer.|
|» » » impact|body|[[CapabilityName](#schemacapabilityname)]|false|Capability codes gated by this requirement, sorted alphabetically. Matches `impact` on the corresponding `GET /v2/customers/{customerId}` requirement entry. Omit when `status` is `cleared`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» » » status|past_due|
|» » » status|pending|
|» » » status|rejected|
|» » » status|cleared|

|» » » impact|custodyFiat|
|» » » impact|custodyStablecoin|
|» » » impact|tradeCrypto|
|» » » impact|tradeStablecoin|
|» » » impact|transferCrypto|
|» » » impact|transferFiat|
|» » » impact|transferStablecoin|

# Schemas

<h2 id="tocS_AccountType">AccountType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccounttype"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountType"></a>
<a id="tocSaccounttype"></a>
<a id="tocsaccounttype"></a>

```json
"prime"
```

The type of the Account.

- `prime`: a linked Coinbase Prime account.
- `business`: a linked Coinbase Business account.
- `cdp`: a CDP-native account created via this API. Used for accounts created on
  behalf of an Entity and for Customer-owned accounts.

<h2 id="tocS_AccountId">AccountId</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccountid"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountId"></a>
<a id="tocSaccountid"></a>
<a id="tocsaccountid"></a>

```json
"account_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114"
```

The ID of the Account, which is a UUID prefixed by the string `account_`.

<h2 id="tocS_Owner">Owner</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaowner"></a>
<a id="schema_Owner"></a>
<a id="tocSowner"></a>
<a id="tocsowner"></a>

```json
"entity_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114"
```

The Owner ID of the Account.

Owner IDs are UUIDs prefixed with the Owner Type as follows:

* **Entity**: `entity_` - If the Owner is your Entity, e.g. `entity_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114`.

* **Customer**: `customer_` - If the Owner is one of your Customers,
  e.g. `customer_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114`. Customer ownership requires the
  Customer to have the `custodyCrypto`, `custodyFiat`, and `custodyStablecoin`
  capabilities enabled.

```json
"My Business Account"
```

An optional name for the account. Must be 1-64 characters and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and spaces.

Used for accounts created on<br>  behalf of an Entity and for Customer-owned accounts.|

Customer ownership requires the<br>  Customer to have the `custodyCrypto`, `custodyFiat`, and `custodyStablecoin`<br>  capabilities enabled.|

<h2 id="tocS_CapabilityStatus">CapabilityStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacapabilitystatus"></a>
<a id="schema_CapabilityStatus"></a>
<a id="tocScapabilitystatus"></a>
<a id="tocscapabilitystatus"></a>

```json
"active"
```

The status of a capability. Based on recoverability:
- `unrequested`: Capability has not been requested by the customer
- `pending`: Customer can take action to resolve (requirements `due` or `rejected`)
- `active`: Capability is enabled and can be used
- `inactive`: Permanently blocked - no customer action possible

```json
  "status": "active"

```

The current state of a capability for a customer. The `status` field is always
present. When `requested` is `false`, the status will be `unrequested`.

|requested|boolean|true|none|Whether the customer has explicitly requested this capability.|
|status|object|true|none|Current status of the capability. When `requested` is `false`, status is `unrequested`.<br>When `requested` is `true`, status is one of `pending`, `active`, or `inactive`.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_RequirementStatus">RequirementStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequirementstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_RequirementStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSrequirementstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsrequirementstatus"></a>

```json
"due"
```

The current status of a requirement:
- `due`: Must be submitted and no set deadline has passed
- `past_due`: Must be submitted and a set deadline has passed
- `pending`: Submitted, awaiting verification
- `rejected`: Verification failed - customer must resubmit

For a Terms of Service requirement, `past_due` applies if any unaccepted
version has a deadline set in the past. Otherwise the status is `due`,
including when a version has no deadline and requires immediate acceptance,
or when every set deadline is in the future and acceptance is in grace.

When verification passes, the requirement disappears from the response entirely.

<h2 id="tocS_TosVersionId">TosVersionId</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematosversionid"></a>
<a id="schema_TosVersionId"></a>
<a id="tocStosversionid"></a>
<a id="tocstosversionid"></a>

```json
"us_individual_2026-05-29"
```

Stable, opaque identifier for a specific Terms of Service version
(for example, `us_individual_2026-05-29`). The same identifier is
surfaced on `Customer.requirements.tos.tosVersions[].versionId` (the
versions a Customer still needs to accept) and on
`Customer.tosAcceptances[].versionId` (the versions the Customer has
accepted). Treat the value as opaque and submit it verbatim; the
identifier format is stable across API versions, but the set of
valid values grows over time as new Terms of Service versions are
published.

<h2 id="tocS_TermsOfService">TermsOfService</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematermsofservice"></a>
<a id="schema_TermsOfService"></a>
<a id="tocStermsofservice"></a>
<a id="tocstermsofservice"></a>

```json
{
  "versionId": "us_individual_2026-05-29",
  "languages": [
    "en"
  ],
  "url": "https://www.coinbase.com/legal/user-agreements-third-party-provider"
}
```

Metadata for one Terms of Service document a Customer may need to
accept. Each entry represents one logical document (identified by
`versionId`) that may be published in multiple languages —
`languages` lists the BCP 47 language tags the document is available
to view and accept in. An optional `deadline` records the end of a grace
period: a future deadline is non-blocking `due`, an elapsed deadline is
`past_due`, and no deadline means acceptance is required immediately with
status `due`. `url` is the canonical, language-agnostic document URL;
partners append `?lang=<tag>` (where `<tag>` is one of `languages`) to
retrieve a specific translation, and omit the parameter to let the
documentation site choose a default. This API does not serve Terms of
Service body content; this schema describes metadata only.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|versionId|object|true|none|Stable identifier for this Terms of Service document. Submit this<br>value as `versionId` on a `TosAcceptance` to record acceptance.<br>|
|deadline|string(date-time)|false|none|Optional deadline by which the Customer must accept this Terms of<br>Service version, in ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 format. A future deadline is<br>non-blocking grace with requirement status `due`; an elapsed deadline<br>produces `past_due`. When omitted, acceptance is required immediately<br>and the requirement status remains `due`.<br>|
|languages|[string]|true|none|BCP 47 language tags this Terms of Service document can be viewed<br>and accepted in. The list is non-empty (every published document<br>carries at least one language). Append the chosen tag to `url` as<br>`?lang=<tag>` to fetch the localized document, and submit the same<br>tag as `language` on the corresponding `TosAcceptance` to record<br>which translation the Customer reviewed.<br>|
|url|object|true|none|Canonical, language-agnostic URL where the Terms of Service<br>document is hosted (for example,<br>`https://www.coinbase.com/legal/user-agreements-third-party-provider`).<br>Append `?lang=<tag>` (where `<tag>` is one of `languages`) to<br>retrieve a specific translation; without the parameter, the<br>documentation site renders a default translation.<br>|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemataxform"></a>
<a id="schema_TaxForm"></a>
<a id="tocStaxform"></a>
<a id="tocstaxform"></a>


Identifier for a tax attestation form a Customer may need to

<h2 id="tocS_Requirement">Requirement</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequirement"></a>
<a id="schema_Requirement"></a>
<a id="tocSrequirement"></a>
<a id="tocsrequirement"></a>

```json
{
  "status": "due",
  "impact": [
    "custodyCrypto",
    "transferCrypto"
  ]
}
```

A single requirement that a customer must submit to enable capabilities.
Requirements are only shown for requested capabilities.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|[RequirementStatus](#schemarequirementstatus)|true|none|The current status of a requirement:<br>- `due`: Must be submitted and no set deadline has passed<br>- `past_due`: Must be submitted and a set deadline has passed<br>- `pending`: Submitted, awaiting verification<br>- `rejected`: Verification failed - customer must resubmit<br><br>For a Terms of Service requirement, `past_due` applies if any unaccepted<br>version has a deadline set in the past. Otherwise the status is `due`,<br>including when a version has no deadline and requires immediate acceptance,<br>or when every set deadline is in the future and acceptance is in grace.<br><br>When verification passes, the requirement disappears from the response entirely.<br>|
|deadline|string(date-time)|false|none|Optional aggregate deadline by which this requirement must be satisfied.<br><br>For the `tos` requirement, this is the earliest set deadline among the<br>unaccepted required Terms of Service versions listed in `tosVersions`.<br>It is omitted only when none of the unaccepted versions has a deadline.<br>Do not infer `past_due` or whether the requirement blocks from this<br>aggregate field alone; inspect each version's deadline.<br>|
|impact|[[CapabilityName](#schemacapabilityname)]|false|none|List of capabilities affected by this requirement, sorted alphabetically.<br>Only present for `due`, `past_due`, `pending`, or `rejected` statuses.<br>|
|tosVersions|[[TermsOfService](#schematermsofservice)]|false|none|Required Terms of Service versions the Customer has not yet<br>accepted, with the metadata needed to render an acceptance UI<br>(each entry carries a stable `versionId`, the BCP 47<br>`languages` the version is published in, an optional per-version<br>`deadline`, and a language-agnostic `url`). A missing deadline means<br>acceptance is required immediately while the requirement status remains<br>`due`; only a set deadline in the past produces `past_due`. This field<br>appears only under the requirement key `tos`; do not infer meaning from<br>`tosVersions` on other requirement keys. Only populated for the `tos`<br>requirement; omitted on every other requirement key. Submit each<br>`versionId` back via `tosAcceptances[].versionId` on `Update Customer`<br>(or `Create Customer`) together with `language` and `acceptedAt` to<br>clear the requirement.<br>|
|taxForms|[[TaxForm](#schemataxform)]|false|none|Required tax attestation forms the Customer has not yet completed.<br>This field appears only under the requirement key `taxAttestation`.<br>Submit each `form` back via `taxAttestations[].form` on<br>`Update Customer` (or `Create Customer`) together with the other<br>fields required for that form to clear the requirement.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|due|
|status|past_due|
|status|pending|
|status|rejected|
|impact|custodyCrypto|
|impact|custodyFiat|
|impact|custodyStablecoin|
|impact|tradeCrypto|
|impact|tradeStablecoin|
|impact|transferCrypto|
|impact|transferFiat|
|impact|transferStablecoin|
|taxForms|us_w9|

<h2 id="tocS_RequirementsMap">RequirementsMap</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequirementsmap"></a>
<a id="schema_RequirementsMap"></a>
<a id="tocSrequirementsmap"></a>
<a id="tocsrequirementsmap"></a>

```json
{
  "firstName": {
    "status": "due",
    "impact": [
      "custodyCrypto",
      "transferCrypto"
    ]
  },
  "fullSsn": {
    "status": "rejected",
    "impact": [
      "custodyCrypto"
    ]
  },
  "ssnLast4": {
    "status": "pending",
    "impact": [
      "custodyCrypto"
    ]
  },
  "sourceOfFunds": {
    "status": "due"
  },
  "citizenship": {
    "status": "due"
  },
  "tos": {
    "status": "due",
    "impact": [
      "transferFiat"
    ],
    "tosVersions": [
      {
        "versionId": "us_individual_2026-05-29",
        "languages": [
          "en"
        ],
        "url": "https://www.coinbase.com/legal/user-agreements-third-party-provider"
      }
    ]
  },
  "taxAttestation": {
    "status": "due",
    "impact": [
      "transferFiat"
    ],
    "taxForms": [
      "us_w9"
    ]
  }
}
```

Map of requirements to be submitted. Each key is the field name
(e.g., "ssnLast4"), with values to describe its state. Requirements
are only shown for requested capabilities. When a requirement is
verified, it disappears from this map.

For the `tos` key, each entry in `tosVersions[]` has its own optional
deadline. The requirement-level `deadline` is an aggregate of those rows:
the earliest set deadline among unaccepted versions, not a separate clock.
A version with no deadline requires immediate acceptance but keeps the
aggregate status `due`. A future deadline is also `due` and represents
non-blocking grace. The aggregate status is `past_due` only when at least
one unaccepted version has a deadline set in the past. Do not infer status
or blocking behavior from omission of the aggregate deadline.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|[Requirement](#schemarequirement)|false|none|A single requirement that a customer must submit to enable capabilities.<br>Requirements are only shown for requested capabilities.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_TosAcceptance">TosAcceptance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematosacceptance"></a>
<a id="schema_TosAcceptance"></a>
<a id="tocStosacceptance"></a>
<a id="tocstosacceptance"></a>

```json
{
  "versionId": "us_individual_2026-05-29",
  "language": "en",
  "acceptedAt": "2026-04-10T12:00:00Z"
}
```

A single Terms of Service acceptance recorded for a Customer. Submit
one entry per required document listed in
`Customer.requirements.tos.tosVersions[]` (returned on `Get Customer`,
`Create Customer`, and `Update Customer`). `language` records the
single translation the Customer actually reviewed.

When new required Terms of Service versions are published, only the
new `versionId`s appear in `Customer.requirements.tos.tosVersions[]`;
submit acceptances for only those new version(s).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|versionId|object|true|none|The `versionId` of the Terms of Service document being accepted,<br>as listed in `Customer.requirements.tos.tosVersions[]`.<br>|
|language|string|true|none|BCP 47 language tag of the Terms of Service translation the<br>Customer reviewed. At write time the server rejects values that<br>are not listed under `languages` on the matching required<br>document for this Customer (same `versionId` as listed in<br>`Customer.requirements.tos.tosVersions[]`).<br>|
|acceptedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp at which the Customer accepted the Terms of Service,<br>in ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 format. The server may validate or reject<br>obviously non-credible timestamps; when enforcement tightens,<br>the authoritative acceptance time may be recorded server-side<br>instead of trusting client-supplied values alone.<br>|

Only contact-identity fields are<br>echoed back; every other field accepted on the `IndividualInput` object<br>(`address`, `ssnLast4`, `dateOfBirth`, `fullSsn`, `citizenship`,<br>`phoneNumber`, and the CDD fields) is ingestion-only and never returned.<br>|

|tosAcceptances|[[TosAcceptance](#schematosacceptance)]|false|none|Terms of Service acceptances recorded for the customer.<br>|

<a id="schemaphysicaladdress"></a>
<a id="schema_PhysicalAddress"></a>
<a id="tocSphysicaladdress"></a>
<a id="tocsphysicaladdress"></a>

```json
{
  "line1": "123 Market St",
  "line2": "Suite 400",
  "city": "San Francisco",
  "state": "CA",
  "postCode": "94105",
  "countryCode": "US"
}
```

A physical address with standard address components including street, city, state/province, postal code, and country.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|line1|string|false|none|Primary street address.|
|line2|string|false|none|Secondary address information.|
|city|string|false|none|City or locality.|
|state|string|false|none|State, province, or region.|
|postCode|string|false|none|Postal or ZIP code.|
|countryCode|string|false|none|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (2 characters). See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_3166_country_codes.|

<h2 id="tocS_DateOfBirthLenient">DateOfBirthLenient</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadateofbirthlenient"></a>
<a id="schema_DateOfBirthLenient"></a>
<a id="tocSdateofbirthlenient"></a>
<a id="tocsdateofbirthlenient"></a>

```json
{
  "day": "15",
  "month": "08",
  "year": "1990"
}
```

Date of birth with lenient formatting. Accepts both zero-padded ("04", "07")
and single-digit ("4", "7") values for day and month.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|day|string|false|none|Day of birth (1-31). Both single-digit ("7") and zero-padded ("07") formats are accepted.|
|month|string|false|none|Month of birth (1-12). Both single-digit ("4") and zero-padded ("04") formats are accepted.|
|year|string|false|none|Year of birth (four digits).|

<h2 id="tocS_IndividualInput">IndividualInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindividualinput"></a>
<a id="schema_IndividualInput"></a>
<a id="tocSindividualinput"></a>
<a id="tocsindividualinput"></a>

```json
{
  "firstName": "Jane",
  "lastName": "Doe",
  "address": {
    "line1": "500 Main St",
    "city": "Boston",
    "state": "MA",
    "postCode": "02108",
    "countryCode": "US"
  },
  "ssnLast4": "6789",
  "dateOfBirth": {
    "day": "15",
    "month": "08",
    "year": "1990"
  },
  "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "phoneNumber": "+15551234567"
}
```

Individual customer data submitted on create / update requests. Fields are
organized by the capabilities they unlock; not all are required for all
customers (the requirements depend on which capabilities are requested).
Read responses return the narrower `Individual` object (only `firstName`,
`lastName`, and `email`), not this full request shape.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|firstName|string|false|none|First name (given name).|
|lastName|string|false|none|Last name (family name/surname).|
|address|object|false|none|Primary residential address. Only US addresses are currently<br>supported. Non-US `countryCode` values are rejected with a 400.<br>|
|ssnLast4|string|false|none|Last 4 digits of the Social Security Number (US only).<br>Used for identity verification.<br>|
|dateOfBirth|object|false|none|Date of birth.|
|fullSsn|string|false|none|Full Social Security Number (US only).<br>|
|citizenship|object|false|none|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code representing the customer's citizenship.<br>|
|email|object|false|none|Email address for the customer.|
|phoneNumber|object|false|none|Phone number in [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format.|
|purposeOfAccount|string|false|none|Primary purpose for using Coinbase services.<br>|
|sourceOfFunds|string|false|none|Primary source of funds for the account.<br>|
|employmentStatus|string|false|none|Current employment status.<br>|
|occupation|string|false|none|Industry or occupation.<br>|
|expectedVolume|string|false|none|Expected annual volume of activity on the account, expressed as a<br>dollar range. Use the dollar-honest ids below:<br><br>- `under_1k`: $0 – $1,000<br>- `1k_to_10k`: $1,000 – $10,000<br>- `10k_to_100k`: $10,000 – $100,000<br>- `100k_to_250k`: $100,000 – $250,000<br>- `250k_to_750k`: $250,000 – $750,000<br>- `750k_to_1_5m`: $750,000 – $1.5M<br>- `1_5m_plus`: $1.5M+<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_UsW9Attestation">UsW9Attestation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemausw9attestation"></a>
<a id="schema_UsW9Attestation"></a>
<a id="tocSusw9attestation"></a>
<a id="tocsusw9attestation"></a>

```json
{
  "form": "us_w9",
  "isExemptBackupWithholding": true,
  "edeliveryConsent": true,
  "acceptedAt": "2026-04-17T20:00:00Z"
}
```

Tax attestation for IRS Form W-9, used for US persons. Carries the
W-9-specific backup withholding certification alongside the fields common
to every form (`edeliveryConsent`, `acceptedAt`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|form|string|true|none|The tax form being attested to, as listed in<br>`Customer.requirements.taxAttestation.taxForms[]`. Must be `us_w9`<br>for this variant.<br>|
|edeliveryConsent|boolean|true|none|Whether the Customer consents to electronic delivery (e-delivery) of<br>tax documents. Both `true` and `false` are recorded as submitted.<br>|
|acceptedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp at which the Customer completed the tax attestation, in<br>ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 format. The server may reject obviously<br>non-credible timestamps.<br>|
|isExemptBackupWithholding|boolean|true|none|Whether the Customer is exempt from backup withholding, as certified<br>on IRS Form W-9.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|form|us_w9|

<h2 id="tocS_TaxAttestation">TaxAttestation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemataxattestation"></a>
<a id="schema_TaxAttestation"></a>
<a id="tocStaxattestation"></a>
<a id="tocstaxattestation"></a>

```json
{
  "form": "us_w9",
  "isExemptBackupWithholding": true,
  "edeliveryConsent": true,
  "acceptedAt": "2026-04-17T20:00:00Z"
}
```

A single tax attestation recorded for a Customer. Submit one entry per
required form listed in `Customer.requirements.taxAttestation.taxForms[]`
(returned on `Get Customer`, `Create Customer`, and `Update Customer`
whenever a `taxAttestation` requirement is unsatisfied). The `form` field
selects the variant and determines which additional fields are required.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[UsW9Attestation](#schemausw9attestation)|false|none|Tax attestation for IRS Form W-9, used for US persons. Carries the<br>W-9-specific backup withholding certification alongside the fields common<br>to every form (`edeliveryConsent`, `acceptedAt`).<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomerWriteBase">CustomerWriteBase</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomerwritebase"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomerWriteBase"></a>
<a id="tocScustomerwritebase"></a>
<a id="tocscustomerwritebase"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "individual",
  "capabilities": {},
  "individual": {
    "firstName": "Jane",
    "lastName": "Doe"
  },
  "projectIds": [],
  "tosAcceptances": [
    {
      "versionId": "us_individual_2026-05-29",
      "language": "en",
      "acceptedAt": "2026-04-10T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "taxAttestations": [
    {
      "form": "us_w9",
      "isExemptBackupWithholding": true,
      "edeliveryConsent": true,
      "acceptedAt": "2026-04-17T20:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "compliance": {
    "requesterIpAddress": "203.0.113.42"
  }
}
```

Fields accepted on customer create and update requests. Shared by
`CreateCustomerRequest` and `UpdateCustomerRequest`; excludes the
server-managed response-only fields that appear on `Customer`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|object|false|none|The type of the customer. Required on create; accepted but ignored on<br>update.<br>|
|capabilities|object|false|none|Capabilities to request for the customer.|
|individual|object|false|none|Information about an Individual customer. Not all fields are required<br>for all customers; the requirements depend on which capabilities are<br>requested. Submit only fields that are required by the capabilities<br>that have been requested.<br>|
|projectIds|[[ProjectId](#schemaprojectid)]|false|none|The project IDs that this customer is associated with.|
|tosAcceptances|[[TosAcceptance](#schematosacceptance)]|false|none|Terms of Service acceptances to record on the customer. Submit one<br>entry per required version surfaced inline on<br>`requirements.tos.tosVersions[]` (returned by `Get Customer`,<br>`Create Customer`, and `Update Customer` whenever a `tos` requirement<br>is unsatisfied). The server rejects each acceptance whose `language`<br>is not listed under `languages` on the matching required version with<br>`errorType: "unsupported_tos_language"`.<br><br>When new required Terms of Service versions are published, only the<br>new `versionId`s appear in `requirements.tos.tosVersions[]`; submit<br>acceptances for only those new version(s).<br><br>Omit `tosAcceptances` on a partial update to leave previously recorded<br>acceptances unchanged. Sending `tosAcceptances: []` is invalid<br>(`errorType: "invalid_request"`) because it would clear all acceptances<br>without replacing them; omit the field entirely when you are not<br>updating Terms of Service acceptances.<br>|
|taxAttestations|[[TaxAttestation](#schemataxattestation)]|false|write-only|Tax attestations to record on the customer. Submit one entry per<br>required form surfaced inline on<br>`requirements.taxAttestation.taxForms[]` (returned by `Get Customer`,<br>`Create Customer`, and `Update Customer` whenever a `taxAttestation`<br>requirement is unsatisfied). The required fields per entry depend on<br>`form`; see `TaxAttestation`. This field is ingestion-only and is<br>never returned on read.<br><br>Omit `taxAttestations` on a partial update to leave previously<br>recorded attestations unchanged. Sending `taxAttestations: []` is<br>invalid (`errorType: "invalid_request"`) because it would clear all<br>attestations without replacing them; omit the field entirely when you<br>are not updating tax attestations.<br>|
|compliance|[Compliance](#schemacompliance)|false|none|Compliance context for a request. Carries per-request compliance signals,<br>such as the IP address of the individual (i.e., end-customer) that<br>initiated the request.<br><br>This object is request-only — it is never echoed back in responses.<br>Inner fields are write-only.<br>|

Submit one<br>entry per required version surfaced inline on<br>`requirements.tos.tosVersions[]` (returned by `Get Customer`,<br>`Create Customer`, and `Update Customer` whenever a `tos` requirement<br>is unsatisfied).   },

```json
    "type": "network",
    "amount": "0.01",

  }

```

The fees associated with this transfer. Different transfer types have different fee structures.

**NOTE:** These examples are not exhaustive.

Common examples:
* **Crypto transfers**: Network fees (gas) paid in the native token
* **Fiat conversions**: Processing fees + exchange fees in USD
* **Wire transfers**: Wire fees ($15) + processing fees ($5) in USD
* **Crypto conversions**: Spread fees paid in the source asset.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferEstimate">TransferEstimate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferestimate"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferEstimate"></a>
<a id="tocStransferestimate"></a>
<a id="tocstransferestimate"></a>

```json
{
  "exchangeRate": {
    "sourceAsset": "usdc",
    "targetAsset": "eur",
    "rate": "0.85"
  },
  "targetAmount": "85.00",
  "targetAsset": "eur",
  "fees": [
    {
      "type": "conversion",
      "amount": "0.01",
      "asset": "usdc"
    }
  ],
  "estimatedAt": "2023-10-08T14:30:00Z"
}
```

Captures estimated values for transfers where amounts can't be guaranteed (e.g., USDC -> EURC).

The values in `estimate` are not modified after a transfer is executed. They are preserved as an immutable record of the original pre-execution snapshot.

The actual executed values are populated in the `transfer` resource post-execution.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exchangeRate|[TransferExchangeRate](#schematransferexchangerate)|false|none|The estimated exchange rate at the time this estimate was captured.|
|targetAmount|string|false|none|Estimated amount of the target asset that will be received, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination.|
|targetAsset|object|false|none|The asset symbol of the estimated target amount.|
|fees|[TransferFees](#schematransferfees)|false|none|The estimated fees at the time this estimate was captured.|
|estimatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when this estimate was captured.|

```json
  "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:05:00Z"
}
```

A Transfer represents all the information needed to execute a transfer and tracks the lifecycle of a transfer from initiation through completion or failure.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transferId|string|false|none|The ID of the transfer. Required when validateOnly is false.|
|status|[TransferStatus](#schematransferstatus)|false|none|The current status of the transfer, indicating what action you need to take next. Required when validateOnly is false.|
|source|[TransferSource](#schematransfersource)|true|none|The source of the transfer.|
|target|[TransferTarget](#schematransfertarget)|true|none|The target of the transfer.|
|sourceAmount|string|false|none|The amount of the source asset that will be transferred out, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination.|
|sourceAsset|object|false|none|The asset symbol of the source amount.|
|targetAmount|string|false|none|The amount of the target asset received, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination. May be omitted in the `quoted` state if the value cannot be guaranteed; see `estimate.targetAmount` for the expected value. Populated with the actual executed amount once the transfer completes.|
|targetAsset|object|false|none|The asset symbol of the target amount.|
|exchangeRate|[TransferExchangeRate](#schematransferexchangerate)|false|none|Exchange rate information for currency conversion. The rate indicates how much of the target asset is equivalent to one unit of the source asset. May be omitted in the `quoted` state if the rate cannot be guaranteed; see `estimate.exchangeRate` for the expected rate. Populated with the actual executed rate once the transfer completes.|
|fees|[TransferFees](#schematransferfees)|false|none|The fees associated with this transfer. Different transfer types have different fee structures. May be omitted in the `quoted` state if the fees cannot be guaranteed; see `estimate.fees` for the expected fees. Populated with the actual fees once the transfer completes.|
|estimate|[TransferEstimate](#schematransferestimate)|false|none|Captures estimated values for transfers where amounts can't be guaranteed (e.g., USDC -> EURC).<br><br>The values in `estimate` are not modified after a transfer is executed. They are preserved as an immutable record of the original pre-execution snapshot.<br><br>The actual executed values are populated in the `transfer` resource post-execution.|
|completedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time the transfer was completed.|
|failureReason|string|false|none|The reason for failure, if the transfer failed. Only present when status is `failed`.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time when this transfer will expire if not executed. Only present for `quoted` status. A new transfer must be created to obtain an updated quote after expiration. Required when validateOnly is false.|
|executedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time the transfer was executed and moved to processing. Only present when status has progressed beyond `quoted`.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time the transfer was created. Required when validateOnly is false.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time the transfer was last updated. Required when validateOnly is false.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|details|[TransferDetails](#schematransferdetails)|false|none|Additional details about the transfer. For example, if the transfer was sent to a deposit destination, the information about that destination will be included in this field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|quoted|
|status|processing|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|

<h2 id="tocS_IsIntermediary">IsIntermediary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaisintermediary"></a>
<a id="schema_IsIntermediary"></a>
<a id="tocSisintermediary"></a>
<a id="tocsisintermediary"></a>

```json
true
```

Indicates whether **Coinbase is acting as the intermediary Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP)**, and your organization is acting as an originating VASP on behalf of your own end customer.

**Background:**

The Travel Rule (FATF Recommendation 16) requires VASPs to collect and share certain information about virtual asset transfers. If your organization is a VASP, and you are acting on behalf of your end customer, you must provide additional Travel Rule data to satisfy compliance requirements.

**Set to `true` when** your organization is itself a VASP acting on behalf of your own end customer (the true originator).

**Set to `false` (or omit) when** your organization is not itself a VASP acting on behalf of an end customer — for example, if the virtual assets involved are your organization's own funds.

**Impact on required fields:**

When `isIntermediary` is `true`, you must provide the `originator` object with the following details:
- The originator's (i.e. your end customer's) name
- The originator's address
- Your organization's VASP information (`virtualAssetServiceProvider` object with `identifier`, `name`, and `address`)

In certain jurisdictions, `personalId` and `dateOfBirth` must also reflect the **original sender's** identity — not your organization's. These fields will not be auto-populated from any internal KYC data when `isIntermediary` is `true`.
