### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|isSelf|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the user attests that the receiving wallet belongs to them.|
|isIntermediary|[IsIntermediary](#schemaisintermediary)|false|none|Indicates whether **Coinbase is acting as the intermediary Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP)**, and your organization is acting as an originating VASP on behalf of your own end customer.<br><br>**Background:**<br><br>The Travel Rule (FATF Recommendation 16) requires VASPs to collect and share certain information about virtual asset transfers. If your organization is a VASP, and you are acting on behalf of your end customer, you must provide additional Travel Rule data to satisfy compliance requirements.<br><br>**Set to `true` when** your organization is itself a VASP acting on behalf of your own end customer (the true originator).<br><br>**Set to `false` (or omit) when** your organization is not itself a VASP acting on behalf of an end customer — for example, if the virtual assets involved are your organization's own funds.<br><br>**Impact on required fields:**<br><br>When `isIntermediary` is `true`, you must provide the `originator` object with the following details:<br>- The originator's (i.e. your end customer's) name<br>- The originator's address<br>- Your organization's VASP information (`virtualAssetServiceProvider` object with `identifier`, `name`, and `address`)<br><br>In certain jurisdictions, `personalId` and `dateOfBirth` must also reflect the **original sender's** identity — not your organization's. These fields will not be auto-populated from any internal KYC data when `isIntermediary` is `true`.<br>|
|attestVerifiedWalletOwnership|boolean|false|none|When `true`, you attest that the beneficiary's wallet ownership has been verified out-of-band. Instructs Coinbase to skip the wallet verification check for this transfer.<br><br>**Only valid when `isIntermediary` is `true`.** You can only attest to the beneficiary's wallet ownership when your organization is acting as the originating VASP on behalf of your end customer, and Coinbase is acting as the intermediary VASP. Returns a `400` error if set to `true` when `isIntermediary` is `false` or omitted.|
|originator|[TravelRuleOriginator](#schematravelruleoriginator)|false|none|Originator (sender) party.|
|beneficiary|[TravelRuleBeneficiary](#schematravelrulebeneficiary)|false|none|Beneficiary (receiver) party.|

A request to create a transfer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|source|[CreateTransferSource](#schemacreatetransfersource)|true|none|The source of the transfer.|
|target|[TransferTarget](#schematransfertarget)|true|none|The target of the transfer.|
|amount|object|true|none|The amount of the transfer, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the asset specified by `asset` (e.g., "100.00" for 100 USD, "0.05" for 0.05 ETH).|
|asset|object|true|none|The symbol of the asset for the amount. This must be one of the assets of the source or target.|
|amountType|string|false|none|Specifies whether the given amount is to be received by the target or taken from the source.<br><br>- `target`: The transfer `target` receives the exact value specified in `amount`. Fees are added to the amount taken from the transfer `source`.<br>- `source`: The transfer `target` receives the value specified in `amount`, minus any fees.<br>|
|validateOnly|boolean|false|none|If true, validates the transfer without initiating it.  If the request is valid, a 2xx will be returned. If the request is invalid, a 4xx error will be returned. The response will include an errorType, for e.g. invalid_target if the specified target cannot receive funds.|
|execute|boolean|true|none|Whether to immediately execute the transfer. If false, the transfer will be created in quoted status and must be executed manually via the /execute endpoint.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|travelRule|object|false|none|Travel Rule compliance information for this transfer. Required for transfers to external wallets above regulatory thresholds. Fields required differ by region and Coinbase contracting entity.|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentExpiries">PaymentExpiries</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentexpiries"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentExpiries"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentexpiries"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentexpiries"></a>

```json
{
  "authorizationExpiresAt": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
  "captureExpiresAt": "2026-01-15T23:59:59.000Z",
  "refundExpiresAt": "2026-02-15T23:59:59.000Z"
}
```

Deadlines for each stage of the payment session lifecycle. All fields are optional; when omitted from a create request, the following defaults apply: `authorizationExpiresAt` = now + 1 day, `captureExpiresAt` = now + 7 days, `refundExpiresAt` = now + 30 days.

Expiries must satisfy `authorizationExpiresAt` ≤ `captureExpiresAt` ≤ `refundExpiresAt`. The API returns a 400 error if this constraint is violated.

Each deadline acts as a guard — after it passes, the corresponding action is rejected, but the session remains in its current status. No automatic state transitions occur; the merchant must take explicit action (e.g., cancel or void) to move the session to a terminal state.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorizationExpiresAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp after which authorization attempts are rejected. Defaults to now + 1 day if omitted. The session remains in its current pre-authorization status; the merchant must explicitly cancel the session.|
|captureExpiresAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp after which capture attempts are rejected. Defaults to now + 7 days if omitted. The session remains in its current status; the merchant must explicitly void to release uncaptured funds.|
|refundExpiresAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp after which refund attempts are rejected. Defaults to now + 30 days if omitted. The session remains in its current status; the refund window is simply closed.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorizationId|object|false|none|The unique identifier of the authorization.|

|amount|string|false|none|A decimal representation of the authorized amount, denominated in the session's `asset`.|

|message|string|false|none|A human-readable message describing the outcome or status for display. Returned for x402 authorizations; omitted for other authorization flows unless documented otherwise.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|externalReferenceId|object|false|none|A merchant-provided internal identifier for this authorization, from the merchant's own system—not visible to the payer. Present only when supplied on the authorization request.|

|source|object|false|none|The payer for this authorization. For wallet authorizations, this is the blockchain address that signed the payloads. For Coinbase authorizations, this is the authenticated Coinbase account. This value is also reflected on the parent payment session's `source` field after a successful authorization.|
|onchainTransactions|[[OnchainTransaction](#schemaonchaintransaction)]|false|none|The onchain transactions associated with this authorization.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the authorization was created.|

<h2 id="tocS_Capture">Capture</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacapture"></a>
<a id="schema_Capture"></a>
<a id="tocScapture"></a>
<a id="tocscapture"></a>

```json
{
  "captureId": "capture_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
  "paymentSessionId": "paymentSession_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "amount": "1.00",
  "finalCapture": true,
  "onchainTransactions": [
    {
      "transactionHash": "0xdef456abc789012345678901234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
      "network": "base"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_12345"
  },
  "createdAt": "2025-06-15T12:20:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-06-15T12:21:00.000Z"
}
```

A collection of authorized funds. Multiple partial captures are allowed up to the authorized amount. Each capture settles funds to the merchant's target.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|captureId|object|false|none|The unique identifier of the capture.|
|paymentSessionId|object|false|none|The ID of the payment session this capture belongs to.|
|status|object|false|none|The current status of the capture.|
|amount|string|false|none|A decimal representation of the captured amount, denominated in the session's `asset`.|
|finalCapture|boolean|true|none|When `true`, this capture is treated as the final one for the authorization. Any remaining capturable balance is released back to the payer immediately after the capture settles. When `false`, the remaining capturable balance stays held and is available for subsequent partial captures (subject to `captureExpiresAt`). Has no effect if `amount` equals the full capturable balance, since no remaining balance exists to release.|
|error|[PaymentError](#schemapaymenterror)|false|none|An error that occurred during a payment operation.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|externalReferenceId|object|false|none|A merchant-provided internal identifier for this capture, from the merchant's own system—not visible to the payer. A manual capture uses the caller-provided value; an auto-capture reuses the authorization's value and omits it when the authorization omitted it. It never falls back to `PaymentSession.externalReferenceId`.|
|customerDisplay|object|false|none|Customer-facing display data for this capture, shown to the payer. A manual capture falls back to the session's `orderCode` when `referenceCode` is omitted; an auto-capture reuses the authorization's `referenceCode`.|
|onchainTransactions|[[OnchainTransaction](#schemaonchaintransaction)]|false|none|The onchain transactions associated with this capture.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the capture was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the capture was last updated.|

Merchant-provided display data shown to the payer during checkout. All fields are informational only — stored and returned as-is, with no effect on payment processing, settlement, or validation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Commonly used when the payer's local currency differs from the settlement currency (e.g., charging in USD but displaying the equivalent in CAD). Stored and returned as-is — no cross-validation is performed against the authoritative `amount` and `asset`. Both `amount` and `currency` must be provided together.|
|orderCode|string|false|none|A customer-visible code for the overall order. When omitted, CDP generates one and returns it. It must not contain personally identifiable information (PII) or payment credentials.|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentSession">PaymentSession</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentsession"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentSession"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentsession"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentsession"></a>

```json
{
  "paymentSessionId": "paymentSession_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
  "entityId": "entity_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
  "amount": "1.00",
  "asset": "usdc",
  "target": {
    "address": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    "network": "base"
  },
  "autoCapture": false,
  "expiries": {
    "authorizationExpiresAt": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
    "captureExpiresAt": "2026-01-15T23:59:59.000Z",
    "refundExpiresAt": "2026-02-15T23:59:59.000Z"
  },
  "status": "created",
  "balances": {
    "capturable": "0",
    "captured": "0",
    "refundable": "0",
    "refunded": "0"
  },
  "url": "https://payments.coinbase.com/payment-sessions/paymentSession_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
  "x402Url": "https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/payment-sessions/paymentSession_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad/authorizations/x402",
  "redirect": {
    "failureUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/payment/failed",
    "successUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/payment/success"
  },
  "customerDisplay": {
    "merchantName": "Acme Store",
    "displayAmount": {
      "amount": "1.37",
      "currency": "cad"
    }
  },
  "externalReferenceId": "merchant-order-abc123",
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_12345",
    "order_reference": "order-67890"
  },
  "createdAt": "2025-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-06-15T12:05:00.000Z"
}
```

Tracks the full lifecycle of a payment from creation through settlement. Typical flow: **Create** → **Authorize** (via payment method) → **Capture**. Optional: **Void** to release uncaptured funds, or **Refund** to return captured funds.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|paymentSessionId|object|false|none|The unique identifier of the payment session.|
|entityId|string|false|none|The ID of the entity that owns the payment session.|
|amount|string|false|none|A decimal representation of the payment amount, denominated in `asset`.|
|asset|object|false|none|The symbol of the asset for the payment amount.|
|target|object|false|none|The target of the payment session.|
|autoCapture|boolean|false|none|When true, a capture is automatically created after a successful authorization. When false or omitted, the merchant must create captures manually via the captures endpoint.|
|expiries|[PaymentExpiries](#schemapaymentexpiries)|false|none|Deadlines for each stage of the payment session lifecycle. All fields are optional; when omitted from a create request, the following defaults apply: `authorizationExpiresAt` = now + 1 day, `captureExpiresAt` = now + 7 days, `refundExpiresAt` = now + 30 days.<br><br>Expiries must satisfy `authorizationExpiresAt` ≤ `captureExpiresAt` ≤ `refundExpiresAt`. The API returns a 400 error if this constraint is violated.<br><br>Each deadline acts as a guard — after it passes, the corresponding action is rejected, but the session remains in its current status. No automatic state transitions occur; the merchant must take explicit action (e.g., cancel or void) to move the session to a terminal state.|
|source|object|false|none|The source of the payment session. Set after a successful authorization. Not present before authorization.|
|status|object|false|none|The most recent meaningful event on the payment session.|
|balances|[PaymentSessionBalances](#schemapaymentsessionbalances)|false|none|Running totals tracking how funds move through the session. All amounts are decimal representations denominated in the session's `asset`.|
|authorizations|[[Authorization](#schemaauthorization)]|false|none|The authorizations for this payment session.|
|captures|[[Capture](#schemacapture)]|false|none|The captures for this payment session.|
|voids|[[Void](#schemavoid)]|false|none|The voids for this payment session.|
|refunds|[[Refund](#schemarefund)]|false|none|The refunds for this payment session.|
|url|object|false|read-only|A URL to the hosted payment page where the payer can complete this payment session.|
|x402Url|object|false|read-only|URL for the hosted x402 payment flow. This endpoint expects an HTTP **POST** request (for example, submitting the x402 payment via request headers); do not treat it as a page opened with GET alone. Only present when the payment target supports a wallet source.|
|redirect|[PaymentRedirect](#schemapaymentredirect)|false|none|Redirect URLs used to direct the payer after a web-based payment flow completes or fails.|
|customerDisplay|[CustomerDisplay](#schemacustomerdisplay)|false|none|Merchant-provided display data shown to the payer during checkout. All fields are informational only — stored and returned as-is, with no effect on payment processing, settlement, or validation.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|externalReferenceId|string|false|none|A merchant-provided internal identifier for this payment session, from the merchant's own system—not visible to the payer. It must not contain personally identifiable information (PII) or payment credentials.|
|cancellationReason|string|false|none|The reason the payment session was canceled. Only present when the session has been canceled.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the payment session was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the payment session was last updated.|

|buyer|object|false|write-only|Information about the person paying. Required by some entity configurations to meet regulatory requirements for fund transfers. When required, omitting this field or leaving required sub-fields empty returns a 400 listing the specific fields needed.|


A request to create a new payment session.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|string|true|none|A decimal representation of the payment amount, denominated in `asset`.|
|asset|object|true|none|The symbol of the asset for the payment amount.|
|target|object|true|none|The target of the payment session.|
|expiries|[PaymentExpiries](#schemapaymentexpiries)|false|none|Deadlines for each stage of the payment session lifecycle. All fields are optional; when omitted from a create request, the following defaults apply: `authorizationExpiresAt` = now + 1 day, `captureExpiresAt` = now + 7 days, `refundExpiresAt` = now + 30 days.<br><br>Expiries must satisfy `authorizationExpiresAt` ≤ `captureExpiresAt` ≤ `refundExpiresAt`. The API returns a 400 error if this constraint is violated.<br><br>Each deadline acts as a guard — after it passes, the corresponding action is rejected, but the session remains in its current status. No automatic state transitions occur; the merchant must take explicit action (e.g., cancel or void) to move the session to a terminal state.|
|redirect|[PaymentRedirect](#schemapaymentredirect)|false|none|Redirect URLs used to direct the payer after a web-based payment flow completes or fails.|
|autoCapture|boolean|false|none|When true, a capture is automatically created after a successful authorization. When false or omitted, the merchant must create captures manually via the captures endpoint.|
|externalReferenceId|string|false|none|A merchant-provided internal identifier for this payment session, from the merchant's own system—not visible to the payer. It must not contain personally identifiable information (PII) or payment credentials.|
|customerDisplay|[CustomerDisplay](#schemacustomerdisplay)|false|none|Merchant-provided display data shown to the payer during checkout. All fields are informational only — stored and returned as-is, with no effect on payment processing, settlement, or validation.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|compliance|object|false|write-only|Compliance context for this payment session. Carries buyer information required by some entity configurations to meet regulatory requirements.|

- `eip3009` — pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the signature.
- `permit2` — pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the signature.
- `erc20_approval` — send `data` via `eth_sendTransaction`, return the transaction hash.
- `spend_permission` — pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the signature.

```json
        }
      }
    }
```

An authorization option for completing payment via a wallet. Specifies the currency, amount, and network the payer would pay on, and the payloads the payer must sign or submit.

|asset|object|true|none|The symbol of the asset the payer would pay in for this option.|
|network|object|true|none|The blockchain network the transaction will occur on for this option.|
|payloads|[[OnchainSignaturePayload](#schemaonchainsignaturepayload)]|true|none|The payloads the payer must sign or submit to authorize the payment via this option.|

<h2 id="tocS_OnchainSignedPayload">OnchainSignedPayload</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaonchainsignedpayload"></a>
<a id="schema_OnchainSignedPayload"></a>
<a id="tocSonchainsignedpayload"></a>
<a id="tocsonchainsignedpayload"></a>

```json
{
  "payloadId": "payload_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
  "signature": "0xabcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890ab"
}
```

A processed onchain payload containing the payload ID and the payer's signature or transaction hash. The `signature` value depends on the original payload `type`:
- `eip3009` / `permit2` / `spend_permission` — a hex-encoded signature from `eth_signTypedData_v4`.
- `erc20_approval` — a hex-encoded transaction hash from `eth_sendTransaction`.
- `solana_subscription` — the 64-byte ed25519 signature for the payer that
  signed, extracted from the signed Solana transaction and base58-encoded.
  Not the signed transaction bytes, and not `0x`-prefixed hex.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payloadId|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the signed payload.|
|signature|string|false|none|The output from processing the payload. For `eip3009`, `permit2`, and `spend_permission` types, this is the cryptographic signature returned by `eth_signTypedData_v4`. For `erc20_approval` types, this is the transaction hash returned by `eth_sendTransaction`. For `solana_subscription`, this is the payer's 64-byte ed25519 signature extracted from the signed Solana transaction and base58-encoded, not the signed transaction bytes or `0x`-prefixed hex.|

<h2 id="tocS_MandateStatus">MandateStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamandatestatus"></a>
<a id="schema_MandateStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSmandatestatus"></a>
<a id="tocsmandatestatus"></a>

```json
"approval_succeeded"
```

The most recent action on the mandate. `status` is an informational indicator of the latest transition; it is not the source of truth for what has durably happened. Read the timestamps for that: `approvedAt`, `canceledAt`, and `revokedAt` each record a durable milestone independently of `status`.

- `created`: the mandate exists but no approval has been attempted. No
  source attached. Not usable.


- `approval_pending`: an approval is in flight. Not usable. Emits
  `acceptance.mandate.approval_initiated`.


- `approval_succeeded`: the mandate has a source and is usable.

- `approval_failed`: the last approval attempt failed. Not usable. Submit
  a new approval to retry.


- `revocation_pending`: a wallet revocation is being confirmed on the
  network. Emits `acceptance.mandate.revocation_initiated`. Resolves to
  `revocation_succeeded` on success or `revocation_failed` on failure.


- `revocation_succeeded`: a wallet revocation removed the spending allowance
  on-chain (`revokedAt` is set). Terminal.


- `revocation_failed`: the last wallet revocation attempt did not complete.
  The spending allowance was not removed, so the mandate remains usable if it
  was usable before. Submit a new revocation to retry.


- `canceled`: the merchant ended the mandate off-chain (`canceledAt` is set).
  The on-chain spending allowance may still be live; a later wallet
  revocation can still move `status` through the `revocation_*` values and
  set `revokedAt`.


**Usable when** `approvedAt` is set, `canceledAt` is null, `revokedAt` is null, and `expiresAt` is null or in the future. Usability is derived from these timestamps, not from `status`: a failed revocation, for example, leaves `status` at `revocation_failed` but the mandate stays usable because the allowance was never removed. Authorization checks the durable conditions in order, and the first match wins: an in-flight approval or revocation returns `409` (`mandate_action_pending`); `revokedAt` set returns `422` (`mandate_revoked`); `canceledAt` set returns `422` (`mandate_canceled`); a past `expiresAt` returns `400` (`mandate_expired`); any other status returns `422` (`mandate_invalid_status`). Approve a mandate and get wallet approval options use that same order for the in-flight, revoked, canceled, and expired checks. Any other status except `created` or `approval_failed` returns `422` (`mandate_invalid_status`). Those rejections do not change the timestamps. Debit limits are enforced at authorization time.

|maxPerAuthorization|string|false|none|Max amount for one authorization. Omit to use the Coinbase default. Capped at the Coinbase ceiling.|
|maxPerPeriod|object|false|none|One rolling cap. Omit to use a Coinbase-configured monthly max. If set, both `amount` and `period` are required. Amount is capped at that period's ceiling.|
|minSetupBalance|string|false|none|Optional minimum available balance the payer must have to set up the mandate, denominated in the mandate's `asset`. When set, the mandate can only be approved if the payer's available balance is at least this amount; an approval attempted while the balance is below it is rejected with a `422` (`mandate_policy_violation`). This does not dictate the amount debited: the payment session amount remains the source of truth for what is debited. Omit to use the Coinbase-configured default.|

<h2 id="tocS_Mandate">Mandate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamandate"></a>
<a id="schema_Mandate"></a>
<a id="tocSmandate"></a>
<a id="tocsmandate"></a>

```json
{
  "mandateId": "mandate_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
  "asset": "usdc",
  "source": {
    "address": "0xAbC1234567890aBcDeF1234567890AbCdEf123456",
    "network": "base",
    "asset": "usdc"
  },
  "policy": {
    "maxPerAuthorization": "50.00",
    "maxPerPeriod": {
      "amount": "500.00",
      "period": "month"
    }
  },
  "status": "approval_succeeded",
  "expiresAt": "2027-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "revocationUrl": "https://payments.coinbase.com/mandates/mandate_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad/revoke",
  "approvalRedirect": {
    "failureUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/approval/failed",
    "successUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/approval/success"
  },
  "revocationRedirect": {
    "failureUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/revocation/failed",
    "successUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/revocation/success"
  },
  "customerDisplay": {
    "merchantName": "Acme Store"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_12345"
  },
  "approvedAt": "2025-06-15T12:05:00.000Z",
  "createdAt": "2025-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-06-15T12:05:00.000Z"
}
```

A durable, revocable standing authorization to debit a funding `source` without the customer present each time, within its `policy` caps. Payment sessions draw against it by referencing its `mandateId`.

`source` is set once an approval succeeds. `status` reflects the most recent action; the `approvedAt`, `canceledAt`, and `revokedAt` timestamps are the durable record of what has happened. Ending one mandate does not affect other mandates on the same `source`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mandateId|object|true|none|The unique identifier of the mandate.|
|asset|object|true|none|The unit of account the mandate's `policy` caps are denominated in (e.g., `500` means 500 of this asset). Fixed at creation. This is only the denomination for the limits; the funding `source` may hold a different asset (for example, limits in `usdc` against a `usdt` source). Each authorization's amount is converted into this asset at authorization time to evaluate the caps, so the caps are always enforced in a single denomination.|
|source|object|false|none|The funding source the mandate draws against. Set when an approval succeeds. Not present before the mandate is `approval_succeeded`.|
|policy|object|true|none|Debit caps. Always present. If you omitted `policy` at create, this is a Coinbase-configured monthly max.|
|status|object|true|none|The current status of the mandate.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp after which the mandate can no longer be authorized against. Authorization attempts after this time return `422`; `status` does not change. Omit for no expiry.|
|url|object|false|read-only|Hosted page where the customer approves this mandate. Present only before the mandate reaches `approval_succeeded`; complemented by `revocationUrl` afterward.|
|revocationUrl|object|false|read-only|Hosted page where the customer can remove their spending allowance for this mandate. Present once the mandate has a `source` (from `approval_succeeded` onward); absent before approval, when there is nothing to revoke.|
|approvalRedirect|object|false|none|Optional merchant URLs used by the hosted mandate approval flow. The approval page redirects to `successUrl` when approval succeeds, or `failureUrl` when it fails. When omitted, the approval page keeps the customer on the Coinbase-hosted experience.|
|revocationRedirect|object|false|none|Optional merchant URLs used by the hosted mandate revocation flow. The revocation page redirects to `successUrl` when revocation succeeds, or `failureUrl` when it fails. When omitted, the revocation page keeps the customer on the Coinbase-hosted experience.|
|customerDisplay|[MandateCustomerDisplay](#schemamandatecustomerdisplay)|false|none|Merchant-provided display data shown to the customer on the hosted mandate pages. All fields are informational only. They are stored and returned as-is and do not affect mandate approval, authorization, or policy enforcement.|
|approvedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which an approval succeeded and the mandate became usable. Present only once the mandate has been approved; set once, on the successful approval, and unchanged by later transitions. Its presence is the durable signal that the mandate was approved, independent of `status`.|
|canceledAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the merchant canceled the mandate off-chain. Present only once the mandate has been canceled. Canceling does not touch the on-chain spending allowance; check `revokedAt` for that.|
|revokedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the spending allowance was removed on-chain by a wallet revocation. Present only once that has happened. Its presence is the single signal that the allowance is gone, independent of `status` (for example, it can be set on a `canceled` mandate whose allowance was later cleaned up).|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the mandate was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the mandate was last updated.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateMandateRequest">CreateMandateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatemandaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateMandateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreatemandaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreatemandaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "asset": "usdc",
  "policy": {
    "maxPerAuthorization": "50.00",
    "maxPerPeriod": {
      "amount": "500.00",
      "period": "month"
    }
  },
  "expiresAt": "2027-06-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "approvalRedirect": {
    "failureUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/approval/failed",
    "successUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/approval/success"
  },
  "revocationRedirect": {
    "failureUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/revocation/failed",
    "successUrl": "https://merchant.example.com/mandate/revocation/success"
  },
  "customerDisplay": {
    "merchantName": "Acme Store"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "cust_12345"
  }
}
```

A request to create a new mandate. The merchant is inferred from the API key. The mandate is returned in `created` status with no source. Attach a source next by approving the mandate, using **Get wallet approval options** then **Approve a mandate with a wallet**, which returns a `pending` approval; the mandate becomes `approval_succeeded` once that approval succeeds. The mandate is denominated in `asset`, fixed at creation. `policy` is optional. Omit it or send `{}` to default to a Coinbase-configured monthly max. The response includes the resolved `policy`. If you set `maxPerPeriod`, include both `amount` and `period`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asset|object|true|none|The unit of account the mandate's `policy` caps are denominated in (e.g., `500` means 500 of this asset). Fixed at creation. This is only the denomination for the limits; the funding `source` may hold a different asset (for example, limits in `usdc` against a `usdt` source). Each authorization's amount is converted into this asset at authorization time to evaluate the caps, so the caps are always enforced in a single denomination.|
|policy|object|false|none|Optional. Omit or send `{}` to default to a Coinbase-configured monthly max. If you set `maxPerPeriod`, include both `amount` and `period`.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp after which this mandate can no longer be authorized against. Omit for a mandate with no expiry.|
|approvalRedirect|object|false|none|Optional merchant URLs used by the hosted mandate approval flow. The approval page redirects to `successUrl` when approval succeeds, or `failureUrl` when it fails. Omit to keep the customer on the Coinbase-hosted experience.|
|revocationRedirect|object|false|none|Optional merchant URLs used by the hosted mandate revocation flow. The revocation page redirects to `successUrl` when revocation succeeds, or `failureUrl` when it fails. Omit to keep the customer on the Coinbase-hosted experience.|
|customerDisplay|[MandateCustomerDisplay](#schemamandatecustomerdisplay)|false|none|Merchant-provided display data shown to the customer on the hosted mandate pages. All fields are informational only. They are stored and returned as-is and do not affect mandate approval, authorization, or policy enforcement.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->


The ID of a revocation, a UUID prefixed by `revocation_`.

<h2 id="tocS_RevocationStatus">RevocationStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarevocationstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_RevocationStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSrevocationstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsrevocationstatus"></a>

```json
"succeeded"
```

The status of a wallet revocation attempt:

- `pending`: awaiting network confirmation.

- `succeeded`: the spending allowance has been removed on-chain.

- `failed`: the revocation did not complete (see `error`).

<h2 id="tocS_Revocation">Revocation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarevocation"></a>
<a id="schema_Revocation"></a>
<a id="tocSrevocation"></a>
<a id="tocsrevocation"></a>

```json
{
  "revocationId": "revocation_9d2e7c14-3b8a-4f21-9c66-2a1e5d7b8f03",
  "mandateId": "mandate_82c879c1-84e1-44ed-a8c2-1ac239cf09ad",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "onchainTransactions": [
    {
      "transactionHash": "0xdef456789012345678901234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890ab",
      "network": "base"
    }
  ],
  "createdAt": "2026-08-21T14:10:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-21T14:12:00.000Z"
}
```

A record of a wallet revocation: the customer removing the mandate's spending allowance on-chain (see `onchainTransactions`). While it is confirming, the mandate's `status` is `revocation_pending`; on success it becomes `revocation_succeeded` and the mandate's `revokedAt` is set, and on failure it becomes `revocation_failed`. This applies regardless of whether the mandate was previously canceled: a revocation on an already-canceled mandate still moves `status` through the `revocation_*` values and sets `revokedAt`.

To check whether the spending allowance is still active, read the mandate: `revokedAt` is set once the allowance has been removed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|revocationId|object|true|none|The unique identifier of the revocation.|
|mandateId|object|true|none|The unique identifier of the mandate this revocation applies to.|
|status|object|true|none|The current status of the revocation attempt.|
|onchainTransactions|[[OnchainTransaction](#schemaonchaintransaction)]|false|none|Network transactions that remove the spending allowance on-chain. Empty until the revocation has been submitted to the network.|
|error|object|false|none|Details of why the revocation failed. Only present when `status` is `failed`.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the revocation was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the revocation was last updated.|

|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|

```json
          "type": "uint256"
        },
        {

          "type": "uint256"
        },

          "type": "uint256"
        }
```

```json
    },
    "primaryType": "Permit",
    "domain": {
      "name": "USD Coin",
      "version": "2",
      "chainId": 8453,
      "verifyingContract": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913"
    },
    "message": {
      "owner": "0xAbC1234567890aBcDeF1234567890AbCdEf123456",
      "spender": "0x9Fb909eA400c2b8D99Be292DADf07e63B814527c",
      "value": "115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935",
      "nonce": "0",
      "deadline": "1798761600"
    }
  }
}
```

A single payload the customer signs to remove the mandate's spending allowance on-chain. Each payload sets the allowance to zero using the same credential type that granted it. Inspect `type` to determine how to handle `data`:

- `eip2612`: an EIP-2612 `Permit` with `value` of `0`; pass `data` to
  `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the signature.


- `permit2`: a Permit2 `PermitSingle` with `amount` of `0`; pass `data` to
  `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the signature.


- `erc20_approval`: an ERC-20 `approve` of `0`; send `data` via
  `eth_sendTransaction`, return the transaction hash.

- `solana_subscription`: decode `data.transaction` from base64 and pass the
  bytes to the Solana Wallet Standard `signTransaction` method (never
  `signAndSendTransaction`). The transaction is `revokeDelegation`.
  From the signed transaction, extract the 64-byte ed25519 signature for
  the payer that signed, base58-encode it, and return that string as
  `OnchainSignedPayload.signature`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[EIP2612Payload](#schemaeip2612payload)|false|none|An EIP-2612 Permit typed-data payload. The payer must pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4` and return the resulting signature. Used to set up a mandate's reusable credential; the permit stands in for a live per-authorization signature on later authorizations.|
|*oneOf*|[Permit2AllowancePayload](#schemapermit2allowancepayload)|false|none|A Permit2 `PermitSingle` (AllowanceTransfer) typed-data payload. It grants the spender a reusable allowance through the canonical Permit2 contract, so it can back repeated charges rather than a single transfer. The payer must pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4` and return the resulting signature. A one-time ERC-20 approval of the Permit2 contract (an `erc20_approval` payload) is required first if the wallet has not yet approved Permit2 for this asset.|
|*oneOf*|[Erc20ApprovalPayload](#schemaerc20approvalpayload)|false|none|An ERC-20 approval transaction payload. The payer must send `data` as an EVM transaction via `eth_sendTransaction` and return the resulting transaction hash.|
|*oneOf*|[SolanaSubscriptionPayload](#schemasolanasubscriptionpayload)|false|none|An unsigned Solana transaction the payer must sign to approve or revoke a mandate on a Solana wallet source. Decode `data.transaction` from base64 and pass the bytes to the Solana Wallet Standard `signTransaction` method (never `signAndSendTransaction`). Do not submit the signed transaction bytes. From the signed transaction, take the 64-byte ed25519 signature for the payer that signed, base58-encode those 64 bytes, and return that string as `OnchainSignedPayload.signature`.|

<h2 id="tocS_ApprovalStatus">ApprovalStatus</h2>

<a id="tocSapprovalstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsapprovalstatus"></a>

```json
"succeeded"
```

The status of an approval attempt:

- `pending`: the submitted source is being bound and verified.

- `succeeded`: the mandate's `source` is attached and its status becomes
  `approval_succeeded`.


- `failed`: the attempt could not be completed (see `error`). The mandate's
  status becomes `approval_failed`; submit a new approval to retry (which
  moves it back to `approval_pending`).

<h2 id="tocS_Approval">Approval</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapproval"></a>
<a id="schema_Approval"></a>
<a id="tocSapproval"></a>
<a id="tocsapproval"></a>

```json
{
  "approvalId": "approval_5f0e9d8c-7b6a-4321-fedc-ba0987654321",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "source": {
    "address": "0xAbC1234567890aBcDeF1234567890AbCdEf123456",
    "network": "base",
    "asset": "usdc"
  },
  "onchainTransactions": [
    {
      "transactionHash": "0xabc123def456789012345678901234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef123456",
      "network": "base"
    }
  ],
  "createdAt": "2025-06-15T12:04:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-06-15T12:05:00.000Z"
}
```

An attempt to attach a funding source to a mandate and make it usable. A successful approval sets the mandate's `source` and moves the mandate to `approval_succeeded`; a failed one moves the mandate to `approval_failed` and can be retried by submitting a new approval. A mandate holds at most one active source, so at most one approval ever succeeds. The network transactions that grant the spending allowance are on `onchainTransactions`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|approvalId|object|true|none|The unique identifier of the approval.|
|status|object|true|none|The current status of the approval attempt.|
|source|object|false|none|The funding source this approval binds to the mandate. Present once the source has been determined from the customer's submission.|
|onchainTransactions|[[OnchainTransaction](#schemaonchaintransaction)]|false|none|Network transactions that grant the spending allowance on-chain. Empty until the approval has been submitted to the network.|
|error|object|false|none|Details of why the approval failed. Only present when `status` is `failed`.|
|metadata|[Metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Optional metadata as key-value pairs. Use this to store additional structured information on a resource, such as customer IDs, order references, or any application-specific data. Up to 10 key/value pairs may be provided. Keys and values are both strings. Keys must be ≤ 40 characters; values must be ≤ 500 characters.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the approval was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the approval was last updated.|

A single payload the customer signs to approve a mandate on a wallet source. Mandates support allowance-style credentials only, since a mandate must be reusable for later debits when the customer is not present. Inspect `type` to determine how to handle `data`:

- `eip2612`: pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the signature.

- `permit2`: a Permit2 `PermitSingle` (AllowanceTransfer) granting a
  reusable allowance; pass `data` to `eth_signTypedData_v4`, return the
  signature. Preceded by a one-time `erc20_approval` of the Permit2 contract
  when the wallet has not yet approved Permit2 for this asset.


- `erc20_approval`: send `data` via `eth_sendTransaction`, return the transaction hash.
- `solana_subscription`: decode `data.transaction` from base64 and pass the
  bytes to the Solana Wallet Standard `signTransaction` method (never
  `signAndSendTransaction`). From the signed transaction, extract the
  64-byte ed25519 signature for the payer that signed, base58-encode it,
  and return that string as `OnchainSignedPayload.signature`. Do not
  submit the signed transaction bytes.

A one-time ERC-20 approval of the Permit2 contract (an `erc20_approval` payload) is required first if the wallet has not yet approved Permit2 for this asset.|
|*oneOf*|[Erc20ApprovalPayload](#schemaerc20approvalpayload)|false|none|An ERC-20 approval transaction payload. The payer must send `data` as an EVM transaction via `eth_sendTransaction` and return the resulting transaction hash.|
|*oneOf*|[SolanaSubscriptionPayload](#schemasolanasubscriptionpayload)|false|none|An unsigned Solana transaction the payer must sign to approve or revoke a mandate on a Solana wallet source. Decode `data.transaction` from base64 and pass the bytes to the Solana Wallet Standard `signTransaction` method (never `signAndSendTransaction`). Do not submit the signed transaction bytes. From the signed transaction, take the 64-byte ed25519 signature for the payer that signed, base58-encode those 64 bytes, and return that string as `OnchainSignedPayload.signature`.|

Adding a new code is a deliberate, coordinated API change; clients receiving an undocumented value should treat it as a server violating the spec.|
|message|string|true|none|A human-readable, English-language description of why this address has no eligible mandate approval option. Suitable for surfacing in product UIs; does not contain personally identifiable information or internal infrastructure details. |fundsRequired|[[WalletMandateApprovalFundsRequirement](#schemawalletmandateapprovalfundsrequirement)]|false|none|The funding options for this address, one entry per (network, asset) combination the customer could fund to become eligible. Only present when `code` is `insufficient_funds`, and honors the request's `network` and `asset` filters. May be an empty array.|

```json
        "network": "base",
        "asset": "usdc"
      },
      "payloads": [
        {
          "payloadId": "payload_af2937b0-9846-4fe7-bfe9-ccc22d935114",
          "type": "eip2612",
          "data": {
            "types": {
              "EIP712Domain": [
                {
                  "name": "name",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                {
                  "name": "version",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                {
                  "name": "chainId",
                  "type": "uint256"
                },
                {
                  "name": "verifyingContract",
                  "type": "address"
                }
              ],
              "Permit": [
                {
                  "name": "owner",
                  "type": "address"
                },
                {
                  "name": "spender",
                  "type": "address"
                },
                {
                  "name": "value",
                  "type": "uint256"
                },
                {
                  "name": "nonce",
                  "type": "uint256"
                },
                {
                  "name": "deadline",
                  "type": "uint256"
                }
              ]
            },
            "primaryType": "Permit",
            "domain": {
              "name": "USD Coin",
              "version": "2",
              "chainId": 8453,
              "verifyingContract": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913"
            },
            "message": {
              "owner": "0xAbC1234567890aBcDeF1234567890AbCdEf123456",
              "spender": "0x9Fb909eA400c2b8D99Be292DADf07e63B814527c",
              "value": "115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935",
              "nonce": "0",
              "deadline": "1798761600"
            }
          }
        }
      ]

  ],
  "ineligibleAddresses": []

```

The available options for approving this mandate on a wallet source, one per eligible asset the address can back. Present them to the customer, have them sign the chosen option's payloads, then call **Approve a mandate with a wallet**. Requested addresses with no eligible option appear in `ineligibleAddresses` with a `code` explaining why. This is a stateless read operation and does not modify the mandate.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|options|[[WalletMandateApprovalOption](#schemawalletmandateapprovaloption)]|true|none|The available wallet mandate approval options.|
|ineligibleAddresses|[[IneligibleWalletMandateApprovalAddresses](#schemaineligiblewalletmandateapprovaladdresses)]|true|none|Requested customer addresses that have no eligible mandate approval option, each with a `code` explaining why. Empty when every requested address can approve the mandate.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateTopUpLinkRequest">CreateTopUpLinkRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatetopuplinkrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateTopUpLinkRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreatetopuplinkrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreatetopuplinkrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "topUpAmount": "100.00",
  "orderTotalAmount": "130.45",
  "asset": "usdc",
  "redirectUrl": "https://www.example-merchant.com/checkout/return?orderId=701-3358192-4471016&sig=8a3f",
  "customerDisplay": {
    "merchantName": "Example Merchant"
  }
}
```

A request to create a Top-Up Link. The entity is inferred from the API key. `topUpAmount` and `asset` are required; `orderTotalAmount`, `redirectUrl`, and `customerDisplay` are optional. Unrecognized top-level fields are allowed and ignored.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|topUpAmount|object|true|none|The merchant-provided initial suggested net amount to add, denominated in `asset`. The suggestion remains fixed on the created link and is not recomputed from `orderTotalAmount` or the payer's current available balance. The payer can adjust the amount they add in the hosted flow. Fiat fees are outside this value. Positive and nonzero, with at most two fractional digits.|
|orderTotalAmount|object|false|none|The total balance, denominated in `asset`, that the merchant expects the payer to need to complete the order. When supplied, the hosted Top-Up page shows the order total and the payer's current available balance, and computes the remaining shortfall from those values. This live shortfall is presentation context: it is separate from `topUpAmount` and does not replace, change, or limit that fixed suggestion.|
|asset|object|true|none|The asset credited by the Top-Up Link. Currently, only `usdc` is supported.|
|redirectUrl|object|false|none|Optional absolute HTTPS URL to which the payer is redirected after the top-up completes. The URL's origin must exactly match one of the entity's configured allowed origins: the HTTPS scheme, hostname (case-insensitive), and effective port (with the default HTTPS port normalized to `443`) are compared, while the path, query, and fragment are ignored. Wildcard or suffix/subdomain matching is not supported. Existing query parameters and the fragment are preserved. The URL must not contain a percent-decoded query key exactly equal to `toppedUpAmount`; every occurrence is rejected, including duplicates, while other casing is allowed. This value can contain sensitive merchant parameters; treat it as secret and do not log it.|
|customerDisplay|[TopUpCustomerDisplayInput](#schematopupcustomerdisplayinput)|false|none|Display details supplied for the hosted Top-Up page. Only the merchant name is supported. Unrecognized fields are allowed and ignored.|

The supplied-name length limit does not constrain the profile-name fallback.|

<h2 id="tocS_TopUpLink">TopUpLink</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematopuplink"></a>
<a id="schema_TopUpLink"></a>
<a id="tocStopuplink"></a>
<a id="tocstopuplink"></a>

```json
{
  "topUpLinkId": "topUpLink_6f2e9b41-c0f4-4bf8-a4b2-c105f9453a24",
  "topUpAmount": "100.00",
  "asset": "usdc",
  "orderTotalAmount": "130.45",
  "redirectUrl": "https://www.example-merchant.com/checkout/return?orderId=701-3358192-4471016&sig=8a3f",
  "customerDisplay": {
    "merchantName": "Example Merchant"
  },
  "topUpUrl": "https://pay.coinbase.com/top-up/topUpLink_6f2e9b41-c0f4-4bf8-a4b2-c105f9453a24",
  "expiresAt": "2026-09-12T20:00:00Z",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-11T20:00:00Z"
}
```

A shareable link that lets a payer add funds to their balance through a hosted Top-Up flow. The resource is immutable once created. The link expires 24 hours after creation and funds a single purchase: once a purchase succeeds, the link is spent and cannot be used again. A purchase that fails does not consume the link, so the payer can retry until it expires. A link is not bound to a specific payer. `orderTotalAmount` and `redirectUrl` are omitted from the response when they were not supplied at creation; they are never returned as null. `customerDisplay` contains the resolved merchant name stored at creation, including the entity's profile name when no nonempty override was supplied. The response and creation webhook always include `customerDisplay` and its `merchantName`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|topUpLinkId|[TopUpLinkId](#schematopuplinkid)|true|none|The ID of the Top-Up Link, a UUID prefixed by `topUpLink_`.|
|topUpAmount|object|true|none|The merchant-provided initial suggested net amount to add for the link's single purchase, denominated in `asset`. The suggestion remains fixed on the link and is not recomputed from `orderTotalAmount` or the payer's current available balance. The payer can adjust the amount they add in the hosted flow. Fiat fees are outside this value.|
|asset|object|true|none|The asset credited by the Top-Up Link. Currently, only `usdc` is supported.|
|orderTotalAmount|object|false|none|The total balance, denominated in `asset`, that the merchant expects the payer to need to complete the order, as supplied at creation. When present, the hosted Top-Up page shows the order total and the payer's current available balance, and computes the remaining shortfall from those values. This live shortfall is separate from `topUpAmount` and does not replace or change that fixed suggestion. It does not limit the amount the payer can add. Omitted when not supplied at creation.|
|redirectUrl|object|false|none|The absolute HTTPS URL to which the payer is redirected after the top-up completes, as supplied at creation. Omitted when not supplied at creation. This value can contain sensitive merchant parameters; treat it as secret and do not log it.|
|customerDisplay|[TopUpCustomerDisplay](#schematopupcustomerdisplay)|true|none|Display details resolved at creation and stored on the immutable Top-Up Link. These details are returned in the create response and creation webhook.|
|topUpUrl|object|true|none|The hosted Top-Up page URL. Share this URL only with the intended payer. The URL identifies the Top-Up Link but does not authorize a purchase; the payer must authenticate and approve the purchase.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp after which the link can no longer be used, 24 hours after creation. A link that has already funded a purchase is spent before this time.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 timestamp at which the Top-Up Link was created.|

```json
{
  "type": "google",
  "sub": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",

  "name": "Test User",
  "username": "test.user"
}
```

Information about an end user who authenticates using a third-party provider.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|[OAuth2ProviderType](#schemaoauth2providertype)|true|none|The type of OAuth2 provider.|
|sub|string|true|none|The unique identifier for the end user that is captured in the `sub` claim of the JWT.|
|email|string|false|none|The email address of the end user contained within the user's ID token, if available from third-party OAuth2 provider's token exchange.|
|name|string|false|none|The full name of the end user if available from third-party OAuth2 provider's token exchange.|
|username|string|false|none|The username of the end user if available from third-party OAuth2 provider's token exchange.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|google|
|type|apple|
|type|x|
|type|telegram|
|type|github|

Information about an EVM account associated with an end user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|string|true|none|The address of the EVM account.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when the account was created, in ISO 8601 format.|
|exportedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The date and time when the account's private key was first exported, in ISO 8601 format. This is set on the first export and preserved on subsequent exports; it is not updated on re-export.|
|ejectedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The date and time when the account's key was ejected (marked for deletion), in ISO 8601 format. Populated when the account has been ejected. The account record remains queryable after this timestamp is set; it reflects when ejection was requested, not when the key material is purged.|

|mfaMethods|[MFAMethods](#schemamfamethods)|false|none|Information about the end user's MFA enrollments.<br>|
|evmAccounts|[string]|true|none|**Deprecated.** **DEPRECATED**: Use `evmAccountObjects` instead for richer account information. The list of EVM account addresses associated with the end user. End users can have up to 10 EVM accounts.|
|evmAccountObjects|[[EndUserEvmAccount](#schemaenduserevmaccount)]|true|none|The list of EVM accounts associated with the end user. End users can have up to 10 EVM accounts.|
|evmSmartAccounts|[string]|true|none|**Deprecated.** **DEPRECATED**: Use `evmSmartAccountObjects` instead for richer account information including owner relationships. The list of EVM smart account addresses associated with the end user. Each EVM EOA can own one smart account.|
|evmSmartAccountObjects|[[EndUserEvmSmartAccount](#schemaenduserevmsmartaccount)]|true|none|The list of EVM smart accounts associated with the end user. Each EVM EOA can own one smart account.|
|solanaAccounts|[string]|true|none|**Deprecated.** **DEPRECATED**: Use `solanaAccountObjects` instead for richer account information. The list of Solana account addresses associated with the end user. End users can have up to 10 Solana accounts.|
|solanaAccountObjects|[[EndUserSolanaAccount](#schemaendusersolanaaccount)]|true|none|The list of Solana accounts associated with the end user. End users can have up to 10 Solana accounts.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when the end user was created, in ISO 8601 format.|

```json
}
```

A capability an asset provides within a borrow product, describing the role the asset plays, either as collateral or debt, and whether that capability is currently active.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The role the asset plays within the product. `collateral` indicates the asset can be posted as collateral, and `debt` indicates the asset can be borrowed.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether this capability is currently active. For example, an asset with a `collateral` capability and `enabled: false` cannot currently be borrowed against.<br>Some venues may temporarily disable an asset's capability, which will be  reflected in the `enabled` field. This would not affect any user's existing  borrow positions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|collateral|
|type|debt|

Morpho Blue's immutable onchain market parameters that uniquely define a borrow product.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|onchainMarketId|string|true|none|The Morpho Blue native bytes32 market ID that uniquely identifies  the underlying market onchain.|
|loanToken|[BorrowProductToken](#schemaborrowproducttoken)|true|none|The token that is borrowed in the product.|
|collateralToken|[BorrowProductToken](#schemaborrowproducttoken)|true|none|The token posted as collateral in the product.|
|oracleAddress|string|true|none|The contract address of the oracle used to price the collateral token against the loan token.|
|interestRateModelAddress|string|true|none|The contract address of the interest rate model that governs the product's borrow rate.|
|lltvBps|integer|true|none|The liquidation loan-to-value of the product, expressed in basis points. For example, `9150` represents an LLTV of 91.5%.|

A borrow product on an EVM network, operated by a lending protocol such as Morpho Blue. 
A borrow product is a protocol-native representation of a borrowable market,  describing the venue that hosts it, the assets that are borrowed or borrowed against  in it, a point-in-time snapshot of its onchain state, and the protocol-specific  immutable parameters that uniquely define it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|borrowProductId|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|none|The globally unique ID of the borrow product, which is a UUID prefixed with the string `bp_`.|
|network|[BorrowProductNetwork](#schemaborrowproductnetwork)|true|none|The name of the EVM network that a borrow product is deployed on.|
|name|string|true|none|A human-readable name for the product, typically derived from its loan and collateral tokens.|
|venue|[BorrowProductVenue](#schemaborrowproductvenue)|true|none|The onchain venue that hosts a borrow product. The venue comprises the protocol and  network the product is deployed on. An example of a venue would be Morpho Blue on  Base Mainnet.|
|assets|[[BorrowProductAsset](#schemaborrowproductasset)]|true|none|The assets available to be borrowed or borrowed against in this market.|
|snapshot|[BorrowProductSnapshot](#schemaborrowproductsnapshot)|true|none|The point-in-time at which onchain state, such as a borrow product or borrow position, was captured. This is when the data was last read from the chain.|
|protocolDetails|[BorrowProductProtocolDetails](#schemaborrowproductprotocoldetails)|true|none|Protocol-specific immutable onchain details that uniquely define a borrow product. The `type` field indicates which protocol-specific schema describes the product's details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|network|base|


The ERC-7677 `context` object forwarded to the paymaster service as part of the `paymasterService` capability. The fields in this object are defined by the paymaster service provider; CDP forwards them to the paymaster unchanged. This field is only valid when a paymaster is configured for the request. Providing `paymasterContext` without a paymaster configured results in an `invalid_request` error.

<h2 id="tocS_BorrowPositionHealthStatus">BorrowPositionHealthStatus</h2>

<a id="schema_BorrowPositionHealthStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSborrowpositionhealthstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsborrowpositionhealthstatus"></a>

```json
"healthy"
```

The aggregate health of a borrow position.

- `no_debt`: the position has no outstanding debt.
- `healthy`: the position has debt and is above its liquidation threshold.
- `undercollateralized`: the position is at or below its liquidation threshold and may be eligible for liquidation.

The live onchain state of a Morpho Blue borrow position, read at the block described by the position's snapshot.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|object|true|none|The protocol type, used to discriminate the onchain state schema.|
|collateral|[[BorrowPositionAssetAmount](#schemaborrowpositionassetamount)]|true|none|The non-zero collateral balances securing the position.|
|debt|[[BorrowPositionDebt](#schemaborrowpositiondebt)]|true|none|The non-zero debt balances owed by the position.|
|healthFactor|string|false|none|The position's liquidation headroom as a decimal string, where `1.0` is the liquidation boundary and higher is safer. For example, `1.79` means the position's weighted collateral is 1.79x its debt. Omitted when the position has no debt.|
|currentLtvBps|integer|false|none|The position's current loan-to-value, expressed in basis points. For example, `5000` represents a current LTV of 50%. Omitted when the position has no debt.|
|liquidationThresholdBps|integer|false|none|The loan-to-value at which the position becomes eligible for liquidation, expressed in basis points. For example, `8250` represents 82.5%. Omitted when the position has no debt.|
|healthStatus|[BorrowPositionHealthStatus](#schemaborrowpositionhealthstatus)|true|none|The aggregate health of a borrow position.<br><br>- `no_debt`: the position has no outstanding debt.<br>- `healthy`: the position has debt and is above its liquidation threshold.<br>- `undercollateralized`: the position is at or below its liquidation threshold and may be eligible for liquidation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|healthStatus|no_debt|
|healthStatus|healthy|
|healthStatus|undercollateralized|

A borrow position held by a smart account in a borrow product, together with its live onchain state read at a point-in-time snapshot.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|borrowProductId|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|none|The globally unique ID of the borrow product, which is a UUID prefixed with the string `bp_`.|
|address|string|true|none|The smart account address that owns the borrow position.|
|network|[BorrowProductNetwork](#schemaborrowproductnetwork)|true|none|The name of the EVM network that a borrow product is deployed on.|
|snapshot|[BorrowProductSnapshot](#schemaborrowproductsnapshot)|true|none|The point-in-time at which onchain state, such as a borrow product or borrow position, was captured. This is when the data was last read from the chain.|
|onchainState|[BorrowPositionOnchainState](#schemaborrowpositiononchainstate)|true|none|The live onchain state of a borrow position. The `type` field indicates which protocol-specific schema describes the state.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|network|base|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateBorrowPositionRequest">CreateBorrowPositionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreateborrowpositionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateBorrowPositionRequest"></a>

<a id="tocscreateborrowpositionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "borrowProductId": "bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df",
  "collateralAmount": "1",
  "loanAmount": "100",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
  "useCdpPaymaster": false,
  "paymasterUrl": "https://api.developer.coinbase.com/rpc/v1/base/AbCdEf123456",
  "paymasterContext": {
    "policyId": "962b252c-a726-4a37-8d86-333ce0a07299"
  }
}
```

A request to create a borrow position for an end user's smart account for the specified borrow product. 
The smart account posts collateral and borrows against it, broadcasting a user operation  to open the position onchain.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|borrowProductId|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|none|The globally unique ID of the borrow product, which is a UUID prefixed with the string `bp_`.|
|collateralAmount|object|true|none|The amount of collateral to post, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the collateral token (i.e. "1" for 1 cbBTC).|
|loanAmount|object|true|none|The amount of the loan token to borrow, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the loan token (i.e. "100" for 100 USDC).|
|walletSecretId|string|true|none|The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth header.|
|useCdpPaymaster|boolean|true|none|Whether to use the CDP Paymaster for the user operation. When `true`, `paymasterUrl` must not be set.|
|paymasterUrl|object|false|none|Paymaster URL to use for the user operation. Must not be set when `useCdpPaymaster` is `true`.<br>If `useCdpPaymaster` is `false` and no `paymasterUrl` is set, the smart account must have sufficient funds to cover network fees.|
|paymasterContext|object|false|none|Optional paymaster metadata forwarded to the configured paymaster service. Valid only when a paymaster is configured via `useCdpPaymaster: true` or a `paymasterUrl`.|

<h2 id="tocS_AdjustBorrowPositionRequest">AdjustBorrowPositionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaadjustborrowpositionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_AdjustBorrowPositionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSadjustborrowpositionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsadjustborrowpositionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "borrowProductId": "bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df",
  "addCollateralAmount": "1",
  "borrowLoanAmount": "100",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
  "useCdpPaymaster": false,
  "paymasterUrl": "https://api.developer.coinbase.com/rpc/v1/base/AbCdEf123456",
  "paymasterContext": {
    "policyId": "962b252c-a726-4a37-8d86-333ce0a07299"
  }
}
```

A request to adjust an existing borrow position for an end user's smart account on the specified borrow product.
The request can supply collateral, withdraw collateral, repay debt, and/or borrow more of the loan asset, broadcasting a user operation to apply the changes onchain.
A single request must not combine `addCollateralAmount` with `removeCollateralAmount` or `repayLoanAmount`, and must not combine `borrowLoanAmount` with `repayLoanAmount` or `removeCollateralAmount`. Otherwise any subset of the four amount fields may be supplied; at least one is required.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|borrowProductId|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|none|The globally unique ID of the borrow product, which is a UUID prefixed with the string `bp_`.|
|addCollateralAmount|object|false|none|The amount of collateral to add to the position, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the collateral token (i.e. "1" for 1 cbBTC). Must not be combined with `removeCollateralAmount` or `repayLoanAmount`.|
|removeCollateralAmount|object|false|none|The amount of collateral to withdraw from the position, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the collateral token (i.e. "1" for 1 cbBTC).  Must not be combined with `addCollateralAmount` or `borrowLoanAmount`.|
|repayLoanAmount|object|false|none|The amount of the loan token to repay, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the loan token (i.e. "100" for 100 USDC).  Must not be combined with `borrowLoanAmount` or `addCollateralAmount`.|
|borrowLoanAmount|object|false|none|The amount of the loan token to borrow, as a decimal string in standard unit denomination of the loan token (i.e. "100" for 100 USDC).  Must not be combined with `repayLoanAmount` or `removeCollateralAmount`.|
|walletSecretId|string|true|none|The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth header.|
|useCdpPaymaster|boolean|true|none|Whether to use the CDP Paymaster for the user operation. When `true`, `paymasterUrl` must not be set.|
|paymasterUrl|object|false|none|Paymaster URL to use for the user operation. Must not be set when `useCdpPaymaster` is `true`.<br>If `useCdpPaymaster` is `false` and no `paymasterUrl` is set, the smart account must have sufficient funds to cover network fees.|
|paymasterContext|object|false|none|Optional paymaster metadata forwarded to the configured paymaster service. Valid only when a paymaster is configured via `useCdpPaymaster: true` or a `paymasterUrl`.|

<h2 id="tocS_CloseBorrowPositionRequest">CloseBorrowPositionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacloseborrowpositionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CloseBorrowPositionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScloseborrowpositionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscloseborrowpositionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "borrowProductId": "bp_07fb56c0-9afe-5440-8ff2-5b0e115458df",
  "walletSecretId": "e051beeb-7163-4527-a5b6-35e301529ff2",
  "useCdpPaymaster": false,
  "paymasterUrl": "https://api.developer.coinbase.com/rpc/v1/base/AbCdEf123456",
  "paymasterContext": {
    "policyId": "962b252c-a726-4a37-8d86-333ce0a07299"
  }
}
```

A request to close an end user smart account's borrow position for the specified borrow product.
Closing fully repays the position's outstanding loan and withdraws all remaining collateral back to the smart account, broadcasting a single user operation to settle the position onchain. There is no partial close; use `adjustBorrowPositionWithEndUserAccount` to adjust a position without closing it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|borrowProductId|[BorrowProductId](#schemaborrowproductid)|true|none|The globally unique ID of the borrow product, which is a UUID prefixed with the string `bp_`.|
|walletSecretId|string|true|none|The ID of the Temporary Wallet Secret that was used to sign the X-Wallet-Auth header.|
|useCdpPaymaster|boolean|true|none|Whether to use the CDP Paymaster for the user operation. When `true`, `paymasterUrl` must not be set.|
|paymasterUrl|object|false|none|Paymaster URL to use for the user operation. Must not be set when `useCdpPaymaster` is `true`.<br>If `useCdpPaymaster` is `false` and no `paymasterUrl` is set, the smart account must have sufficient funds to cover network fees.|
|paymasterContext|object|false|none|Optional paymaster metadata forwarded to the configured paymaster service. Valid only when a paymaster is configured via `useCdpPaymaster: true` or a `paymasterUrl`.|

The x402 v2 network identifier in CAIP-2 format. x402 v2 identifies networks by their CAIP-2 chain ID (e.g. `eip155:<chainId>` for EVM networks, `solana:<genesisHash>` for Solana). Supported networks: Base, Polygon, Arbitrum One, World Chain (EVM), Monad (EVM), and Solana.

<h2 id="tocS_x402V2PaymentRequirements">x402V2PaymentRequirements</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemax402v2paymentrequirements"></a>

<a id="tocSx402v2paymentrequirements"></a>
<a id="tocsx402v2paymentrequirements"></a>

```json
{
  "scheme": "exact",
  "network": "eip155:8453",
  "asset": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
  "amount": "1000000",
  "payTo": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e",
  "maxTimeoutSeconds": 10,
  "extra": {
    "name": "USDC",
    "version": "2"
  }
}
```

The x402 v2 payment requirements. Uses CAIP-2 network identifiers and supports `exact`, `upto`, and `batch-settlement` schemes. Carries only the payment fields (no resource metadata — that is in the enclosing `x402V2PaymentPayload.resource`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheme|string|true|none|The scheme of the payment protocol to use. Supported schemes are `exact`, `upto`, and `batch-settlement`.|
|network|object|true|none|The network of the blockchain to send payment on in CAIP-2 format.|
|asset|object|true|none|The asset to pay with.<br><br>For EVM networks, the asset will be a 0x-prefixed, checksum EVM address.<br><br>For Solana-based networks, the asset will be a base58-encoded Solana address.|
|amount|string|true|none|The amount to pay for the resource in atomic units of the payment asset.|
|payTo|object|true|none|The destination to pay value to.<br><br>For EVM networks, payTo will be a 0x-prefixed, checksum EVM address.<br><br>For Solana-based networks, payTo will be a base58-encoded Solana address.|
|maxTimeoutSeconds|integer|true|none|The maximum time in seconds for the resource server to respond.|
|extra|object|false|none|The optional additional scheme-specific payment info.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|scheme|exact|
|scheme|upto|
|scheme|batch-settlement|

```json
{
  "signature": "0x2d6a7588d6acca505cbf0d9a4a227e0c52c6c34008c8e8986a1283259764173608a2ce6496642e377d6da8dbbf5836e9bd15092f9ecab05ded3d6293af148b571c",
  "permit2Authorization": {
    "from": "0x857b06519E91e3A54538791bDbb0E22373e36b66",
    "permitted": {
      "token": "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e",
      "amount": "5000000"
    },
    "spender": "0x4020A4f3b7b90ccA423B9fabCc0CE57C6C240002",
    "nonce": "12345678901234567890",
    "deadline": "1740672154",
    "witness": {
      "to": "0x209693Bc6afc0C5328bA36FaF03C514EF312287C",
      "facilitator": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
```
